@documentation/guides/PATTERNS_GUIDE.md:508-522 What is this yield call pattern, is this valid javascript?

---

_**Agent (model composer-1, mode Agent)**_


This uses generator functions (`function*`) and `yield`, which are valid ES6 JavaScript. `call` is a Redux-Saga effect creator, not native JavaScript.

## Valid JavaScript parts

1. Generator function syntax (`function*`) — ES6
2. `yield` keyword — pauses execution and returns a value

## Redux-Saga specific parts

`call` is a Redux-Saga effect creator, not native JavaScript. It returns an effect object that the saga middleware interprets.

## How it works

```javascript
// This is valid JavaScript syntax:
function* userRegistrationSaga(action) {
  // yield pauses execution and returns a value
  const validated = yield call(validateUser, action.payload);
  // ↑ This returns an effect object like: { type: 'CALL', fn: validateUser, args: [...] }
  // Redux-Saga middleware intercepts this and actually calls validateUser
}

// Native JavaScript equivalent (without Redux-Saga):
async function userRegistrationSaga(action) {
  const validated = await validateUser(action.payload);
  const user = await createUser(validated);
  await sendEmail(user);
  return { type: 'REGISTRATION_SUCCESS', user };
}
```

## Redux-Saga effects

Redux-Saga provides effect creators:
- `call(fn, ...args)` — calls a function
- `put(action)` — dispatches an action
- `select(selector)` — reads from state
- `take(pattern)` — waits for an action

These return plain objects that the middleware handles.

## Summary

- Valid JavaScript: `function*`, `yield`
- Redux-Saga: `call`, `put` (effect creators)
- Similar to: async/await, but using generators for testability and control

The syntax is valid; `call` is a Redux-Saga utility, not a JavaScript keyword.

          },
          {
            "text": "# Service Factory vs Service Locator: Complete Comparison",

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "## Quick Decision Tree",

          },

            "text": "## Comparison Table",

        "contents": "|--------|----------------|-----------------|--------------------------|\n| **Complexity** | Medium | Medium | Low ✅ |\n| **Boilerplate** | Medium | Medium | Low ✅ |\n| **Access Pattern** | Pass as params | Global container | Pass as params |\n| **Testability** | Excellent ✅ | Good | Good |\n| **Flexibility** | High ✅ | Very High ✅ | Low |\n| **Explicit Dependencies** | Very explicit ✅ | Implicit | Very explicit ✅ |\n| **Best For** | Organized setup | Many consumers | Simple apps |\n| **When Services Needed** | At creation time | Anywhere, anytime | At creation time |\n| **Dependency Tracking** | Easy (import graph) | Hard (hidden) | Easy (import graph) ✅ |\n\n---\n\n## Service Factory Pattern\n\n### What It Is\n\nA function that creates and wires up all services, returning an object of services.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// services/ServicesFactory.js\nexport function createServices(config = {}) {\n  const registry = new Registry();\n  const transitionManager = new TransitionManager({ registry });\n  const router = new Router({ registry });\n  \n  return {\n    registry,\n    transitionManager,\n    router,\n  };\n}\n\n// App.js\nimport { createServices } from './services/ServicesFactory.js';\n\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    this.services = createServices();\n    this.router = this.services.router;\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Use Cases\n\n| Use Case | Example | Why Factory? |\n|----------|---------|--------------|\n| **Complex initialization** | Services need setup, config, wiring | ✅ Factory handles complexity |\n| **Environment-specific config** | Dev vs Prod settings | ✅ Pass config to factory |\n| **Service dependencies** | Registry → TransitionManager → Router | ✅ Factory wires dependencies |\n| **Organized codebase** | Want services separate from app logic | ✅ Clean separation |\n| **Multiple environments** | SSR, testing, production | ✅ Easy to create test services |\n| **Service lifecycle** | Services need initialization order | ✅ Factory controls order |\n\n### Pros\n\n- ✅ **Explicit dependencies** - Clear what's injected\n- ✅ **Easy to test** - Create services with test config\n- ✅ **Organized** - Services creation in one place\n- ✅ **Configurable** - Pass config per environment\n- ✅ **Type-safe** - Can add TypeScript/JSDoc easily\n- ✅ **Testable** - Can create mock services easily\n- ✅ **Clear ownership** - Know where services are created\n\n### Cons\n\n- ❌ **Must pass services** - Need to thread through constructors\n- ❌ **Not available everywhere** - Must pass to where needed",

        "contents": "## Hybrid Approach (Best of Both)\n\nYou can combine both patterns:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// services/ServicesFactory.js - Factory\nexport function createServices(config = {}) {\n  const registry = new Registry();\n  const transitionManager = new TransitionManager({ registry });\n  const router = new Router({ registry });\n  \n  return { registry, transitionManager, router };\n}\n\n// services/ServiceContainer.js - Locator\nexport const services = new ServiceContainer();\n\n// App.js - Use both\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    // Create with factory\n    const appServices = createServices();\n    \n    // Register in locator (for deep access)\n    services.register('router', appServices.router);\n    services.register('transitionManager', appServices.transitionManager);\n    \n    // Inject explicitly (for main components)\n    this.currentPage = new Page({\n      transitionManager: appServices.transitionManager,\n      router: appServices.router,\n    });\n  }\n}\n\n// Deep components use locator\nclass Footer {\n  handleLink(href) {\n    services.get('router').updatePage(href); // ✅ No prop drilling\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**When to use hybrid:**\n- Main components: Explicit injection (clear dependencies)\n- Deep components: Service locator (avoid prop drilling)\n- Best of both worlds!\n\n---\n\n## Recommendation Matrix\n\n| Your Situation | Recommended Pattern | Why |\n|----------------|---------------------|-----|\n| **Small app (&lt; 10 services)** | Direct creation in App.js | Simplest |\n| **Medium app (10-20 services)** | Service Factory | Organized, configurable |\n| **Large app (20+ services)** | Service Factory + Locator | Factory for creation, Locator for access |\n| **Deep component tree** | Service Locator (or Hybrid) | Avoid prop drilling |\n| **Plugin system** | Service Locator | Plugins need access |\n| **Heavy testing** | Service Factory | Easy to mock |\n| **Rapid development** | Service Locator | Fast access |\n| **Long-term maintenance** | Service Factory | Clear dependencies |\n\n---\n\n## For Your Codebase\n\n### Current State\n- Medium-sized app",

        "contents": "    this.routerResolver = this.services.routerResolver;\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Service Factory Pattern\n\nThe &#96;ServicesFactory&#96; (&#96;app/services/ServicesFactory.js&#96;) implements the **Factory Pattern** and **Dependency Injection** to create and wire all services together. This centralizes service creation and ensures proper dependency management.\n\n**Key Benefits:**\n- Single point of service creation\n- Automatic dependency injection\n- Easy to test (can mock services)\n- Clear dependency graph\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// ServicesFactory creates all services with proper dependencies\nexport function createServices() {\n  const siteConfig = new SiteConfig();\n  const animationsService = new AnimationsService();\n  const transitionsService = new TransitionsService({ \n    siteConfig,\n    transitionType: TRANSITION_TYPES.CUSTOM\n  });\n  const smoothScroll = new SmoothScroll();\n  const footnotes = new Footnotes({ smoothScroll });\n  const routerPageLoader = new RouterPageLoader({ siteConfig, smoothScroll, animationsManager: animationsService, transitionsManager: transitionsService, footnotes });\n  const registryService = new RegistryService({ siteConfig, routerPageLoader });\n  const routerPageManager = new RouterPageManager({ siteConfig, routerPageLoader });\n  // ... more services\n  \n  return {\n    siteConfig,\n    router,\n    smoothScroll,\n    animationsService,\n    transitionsService,\n    // ... all services\n  };\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Design Patterns\n\n### 1. Service Factory Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/services/ServicesFactory.js&#96;\n\nCreates and configures all application services with proper dependency injection. Services are created once and shared across the application.\n\n### 2. Registry Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/services/RegistryService.js&#96;\n\nThe &#96;RegistryService&#96; maintains a registry of page classes and their instances.           {
            "text": "## Design Patterns",
            "lineNumber": 95
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 96
          },
          {
            "text": "### 1. Service Factory Pattern",
            "lineNumber": 97
          },
          {
            "text": "**Location:** &#96;app/services/ServicesFactory.js&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 98
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 99
          },
          {
            "text": "Creates and configures all application services with proper dependency injection. Services are created once and shared across the application.",
            "lineNumber": 100
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 101
          },
          {
            "text": "### 2. Registry Pattern",
            "lineNumber": 102
          },
          {
            "text": "**Location:** &#96;app/services/RegistryService.js&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 103
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 104
          },
          {
            "text": "The &#96;RegistryService&#96; maintains a registry of page classes and their instances. It tracks:",
            "lineNumber": 105
          },
          {
            "text": "- Loaded page classes (Map of template → PageClass)",
            "lineNumber": 106
          },
          {
            "text": "- Current page instance",
            "lineNumber": 107
          },
          {
            "text": "- Current page template",
            "lineNumber": 108
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 109
          },
          {
            "text": "**Usage:**",
            "lineNumber": 110
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript",
            "lineNumber": 111
          },
          {
            "text": "// Register a page class",
            "lineNumber": 112
          }
        ]

        "contents": "## For Your Codebase\n\n### Current State\n- Medium-sized app\n- Services: Registry, Router, TransitionManager, SmoothScroll\n- Some services shared, some per-page\n- Testing not yet heavy\n\n### Recommendation: **Service Factory** ✅\n\n**Why:**\n1. ✅ Organized - Clean separation of service creation\n2. ✅ Configurable - Can set dev vs prod settings\n3. ✅ Testable - Easy to create test services\n4. ✅ Explicit - Clear what services are needed\n5. ✅ Future-proof - Easy to add more services\n6. ✅ Not too complex - Simple factory function\n\n**Implementation:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// services/ServicesFactory.js\nexport function createServices(config = {}) {\n  const registry = new Registry();\n  const transitionManager = new TransitionManager({ \n    registry,\n    ...config.transition \n  });\n  const router = new Router({ \n    registry,\n    ...config.router \n  });\n  \n  return {\n    registry,\n    transitionManager,\n    router,\n  };\n}\n\n// App.js\nimport { createServices } from './services/ServicesFactory.js';\n\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    this.services = createServices({\n      transition: { preloadAll: true },\n    });\n    \n    // Inject into pages\n    this.currentPage = new PageClass({\n      transitionManager: this.services.transitionManager,\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

        "contents": "# Architecture Overview\n\n## Table of Contents\n- [Core Architecture](#core-architecture)\n- [Design Patterns](#design-patterns)\n- [Class Hierarchy](#class-hierarchy)\n- [Data Flow](#data-flow)\n- [Key Components](#key-components)\n\n## Core Architecture\n\nThis single-page application (SPA) is built with vanilla JavaScript, following a modular architecture that emphasizes separation of concerns, dependency injection, and a service-oriented design.\n\n### Entry Point\n\nThe application starts at &#96;app/App.js&#96;, which:\n1. Initializes the service factory to create all services\n2. Sets up the router to handle navigation\n3. Creates the preloader for initial page load\n4. Manages the application lifecycle\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// App.js structure\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    this.pageConfig = setupPageConfig();\n    this.preloaderVisible = false;\n  }\n\n  async init() {\n    this.createServices();\n    await this.transitionsService.init();\n    await this.services.router.start(); // Calls pageLoader.create() to initialize the first page\n    this.currentPage = this.services.registryService.getCurrentPage();\n    this.createNavigation();\n    this.createPreloader();\n    liveReload();\n  }\n\n  createServices() {\n    this.services = createServices();\n    this.siteConfig = this.services.siteConfig;\n    this.router = this.services.router;\n    this.navigation = this.services.navigation;\n    this.smoothScroll = this.services.smoothScroll;\n    this.animationsService = this.services.animationsService;\n    this.transitionsService = this.services.transitionsService;\n    this.footnotes = this.services.footnotes;\n    this.pageRegistry = this.services.registryService;\n    this.pageLoader = this.services.routerPageLoader;\n    this.pageManager = this.services.routerPageManager;\n    this.routerHistory = this.services.routerHistory;\n    this.routerResolver = this.services.routerResolver;\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

        "contents": "- ❌ **Hard to test** - Must mock container or clear services\n- ❌ **Magic strings** - Service names are strings (typos)\n- ❌ **No compile-time checking** - Errors only at runtime\n- ❌ **Tight coupling** - Code depends on container\n\n---\n\n## Detailed Comparison\n\n### Dependency Visibility\n\n**Service Factory:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ✅ Explicit - can see dependencies\nclass Page {\n  constructor({ transitionManager, router }) {\n    // Clear what's needed\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Service Locator:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ❌ Implicit - hidden dependencies\nclass Page {\n  constructor() {\n    this.transitionManager = services.get('transitionManager');\n    // Can't tell what services are needed without reading code\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Testing\n\n**Service Factory:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ✅ Easy to create test services\nconst testServices = createServices({\n  transition: { preloadAll: false },\n  router: { mockMode: true },\n});\n\nconst page = new Page({ transitionManager: testServices.transitionManager });\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Service Locator:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ⚠️ Must mock container or clear services\nservices.clear(); // Clear all\nservices.register('transitionManager', mockTM);\nconst page = new Page(); // Uses mocked service\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Access Pattern\n\n**Service Factory:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ✅ Must pass through constructors\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    this.services = createServices();\n  }\n  \n  createPage() {\n    return new Page({ \n      transitionManager: this.services.transitionManager \n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Service Locator:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ✅ Access from anywhere\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    services.register('router', new Router());\n  }\n}\n\nclass Page {\n  constructor() {\n    // ✅ Can access directly\n    this.router = services.get('router');\n  }\n}\n\nclass DeepComponent {\n  // ✅ Can access even here, 5 levels deep\n  handleClick() {\n    services.get('router').updatePage('/home');\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Configuration\n\n**Service Factory:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ✅ Easy to configure\nconst services = createServices({\n  transition: { preloadAll: true },\n  router: { enableLogging: isDev },\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Service Locator:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js",

        "contents": "constructor({ \n    id, \n    element, \n    elements,\n    // ✅ Injected services (shared, stateful)\n    transitionManager,\n    // ✅ Optional - can create if not provided\n    smoothScroll = null,\n    animation = null,\n  }) {\n    this.id = id;\n    this.selector = element;\n    this.transitionManager = transitionManager; // Shared instance\n    \n    // ✅ Stateless utilities can be instantiated\n    this.animation = animation ?? new Animation();\n    \n    // ✅ Per-page services (create if not injected)\n    this.smoothScroll = smoothScroll;\n  }\n  \n  async create() {\n    // ✅ Use shared transition manager\n    // (images already preloaded by first page!)\n    await this.transitionManager.getTransition(route);\n    \n    // ✅ Create per-page service if not injected\n    if (!this.smoothScroll) {\n      this.smoothScroll = new SmoothScroll();\n    }\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Pros and Cons Comparison\n\n### ES6 Imports\n\n**Pros:**\n- ✅ Simple, straightforward\n- ✅ No boilerplate\n- ✅ IDE can track imports easily\n- ✅ Tree-shaking works well\n- ✅ Great for utilities\n\n**Cons:**\n- ❌ Hard to mock in tests\n- ❌ Hard to configure\n- ❌ Can't swap implementations\n- ❌ Creates new instances each time\n- ❌ Hard to share state\n\n### Dependency Injection\n\n**Pros:**\n- ✅ Testable (easy to mock)\n- ✅ Configurable\n- ✅ Share instances (memory efficient)\n- ✅ Swap implementations easily\n- ✅ Clear dependencies\n\n**Cons:**\n- ❌ More boilerplate\n- ❌ Need to wire up dependencies\n- ❌ Can be over-engineered for simple cases\n- ❌ Harder to track \"who uses what\" (no import graph)\n\n### Hybrid (Recommended)\n\n**Pros:**\n- ✅ Best of both worlds\n- ✅ Simple for simple cases\n- ✅ Flexible for complex cases\n- ✅ Good balance of complexity\n\n**Cons:**\n- ⚠️ Need to decide case-by-case\n- ⚠️ Slightly more mental overhead\n\n---\n\n## Composition vs Inheritance\n\n**These are separate concepts!**\n\n- **Composition**: Building complex objects from simpler parts\n- **Inheritance**: Classes extending other classes\n- **DI**: A technique to achieve composition",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./documentation/guides/SERVICES_GUIDE.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 694

        "contents": "- ❌ **Must pass services** - Need to thread through constructors\n- ❌ **Not available everywhere** - Must pass to where needed\n- ❌ **More setup** - Need factory function\n- ❌ **Coupling** - Services must be passed through layers\n\n---\n\n## Service Locator Pattern\n\n### What It Is\n\nA global container that holds services, accessible from anywhere.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// services/ServiceContainer.js\nclass ServiceContainer {\n  constructor() {\n    this.services = new Map();\n  }\n  \n  register(name, service) {\n    this.services.set(name, service);\n  }\n  \n  get(name) {\n    return this.services.get(name);\n  }\n}\n\nexport const services = new ServiceContainer();\n\n// App.js - Register services\nservices.register('registry', new Registry());\nservices.register('router', new Router());\n\n// Anywhere - Access services\nimport { services } from './services/ServiceContainer.js';\nconst router = services.get('router');\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Use Cases\n\n| Use Case | Example | Why Locator? |\n|----------|---------|--------------|\n| **Services needed everywhere** | Navigation, router, event bus | ✅ Access from anywhere |\n| **Deep component tree** | Components 5+ levels deep | ✅ No need to pass through |\n| **Event emitters** | Global event system | ✅ Single instance accessible |\n| **Utility services** | Logging, analytics | ✅ Available anywhere |\n| **Plugin system** | Third-party plugins need services | ✅ Plugins can access services |\n| **Rapid prototyping** | Quick access, less boilerplate | ✅ Fast development |\n| **Legacy migration** | Gradually refactoring old code | ✅ Easy to adopt |\n\n### Pros\n\n- ✅ **Accessible anywhere** - No need to pass through layers\n- ✅ **Flexible** - Services available when needed\n- ✅ **Less boilerplate** - Don't thread through constructors\n- ✅ **Easy for plugins** - Third-party code can access\n- ✅ **Quick development** - Fast to add services\n\n### Cons\n\n- ❌ **Hidden dependencies** - Can't see what services are used\n- ❌ **Global state** - Can become hard to track\n- ❌ **Hard to test** - Must mock container or clear services\n- ❌ **Magic strings** - Service names are strings (typos)",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "- ❌ **Must pass services** - Need to thread through constructors",
            "lineNumber": 695
          },
          {
            "text": "- ❌ **Not available everywhere** - Must pass to where needed",
            "lineNumber": 696
          },
          {
            "text": "- ❌ **More setup** - Need factory function",
            "lineNumber": 697
          },
          {
            "text": "- ❌ **Coupling** - Services must be passed through layers",
            "lineNumber": 698
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 699
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 700
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 701
          },
          {
            "text": "## Service Locator Pattern",
            "lineNumber": 702
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 703
          },
          {
            "text": "### What It Is",
            "lineNumber": 704
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 705
          },
          {
            "text": "A global container that holds services, accessible from anywhere.",
            "lineNumber": 706
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 707
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;js",
            "lineNumber": 708
          },
          {
            "text": "// services/ServiceContainer.js",
            "lineNumber": 709
          },
          {
            "text": "class ServiceContainer {",
            "lineNumber": 710
          },
          {
            "text": "  constructor() {",
            "lineNumber": 711
          },
          {
            "text": "    this.services = new Map();",
            "lineNumber": 712
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 713
          },
          {
            "text": "  ",
            "lineNumber": 714
          },
          {
            "text": "  register(name, service) {",
            "lineNumber": 715
          },
          {
            "text": "    this.services.set(name, service);",
            "lineNumber": 716
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 717
          },
          {
            "text": "  ",
            "lineNumber": 718
          },
          {
            "text": "  get(name) {",
            "lineNumber": 719
          },
          {
            "text": "    return this.services.get(name);",
            "lineNumber": 720
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 721
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 722
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 723
          },
          {
            "text": "export const services = new ServiceContainer();",
            "lineNumber": 724
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 725
          },
          {
            "text": "// App.js - Register services",
            "lineNumber": 726
          },
          {
            "text": "services.register('registry', new Registry());",
            "lineNumber": 727
          },
          {
            "text": "services.register('router', new Router());",
            "lineNumber": 728
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 729
          },
          {
            "text": "// Anywhere - Access services",
            "lineNumber": 730
          },
          {
            "text": "import { services } from './services/ServiceContainer.js';",
            "lineNumber": 731
          },
          {
            "text": "const router = services.get('router');",
            "lineNumber": 732
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 733
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 734
          },
          {
            "text": "### Use Cases",
            "lineNumber": 735
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 736
          },
          {
            "text": "| Use Case | Example | Why Locator? |",
            "lineNumber": 737
          },
          {
            "text": "|----------|---------|--------------|",
            "lineNumber": 738
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Services needed everywhere** | Navigation, router, event bus | ✅ Access from anywhere |",
            "lineNumber": 739
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Deep component tree** | Components 5+ levels deep | ✅ No need to pass through |",
            "lineNumber": 740
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Event emitters** | Global event system | ✅ Single instance accessible |",
            "lineNumber": 741
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Utility services** | Logging, analytics | ✅ Available anywhere |",
            "lineNumber": 742
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Plugin system** | Third-party plugins need services | ✅ Plugins can access services |",
            "lineNumber": 743
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Rapid prototyping** | Quick access, less boilerplate | ✅ Fast development |",
            "lineNumber": 744
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Legacy migration** | Gradually refactoring old code | ✅ Easy to adopt |",
            "lineNumber": 745
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 746
          },
          {
            "text": "### Pros",
            "lineNumber": 747
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 748
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ **Accessible anywhere** - No need to pass through layers",
            "lineNumber": 749
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ **Flexible** - Services available when needed",
            "lineNumber": 750
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ **Less boilerplate** - Don't thread through constructors",
            "lineNumber": 751
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ **Easy for plugins** - Third-party code can access",
            "lineNumber": 752
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ **Quick development** - Fast to add services",
            "lineNumber": 753
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 754
          },
          {
            "text": "### Cons",
            "lineNumber": 755
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 756
          },
          {
            "text": "- ❌ **Hidden dependencies** - Can't see what services are used",
            "lineNumber": 757
          },
          {
            "text": "- ❌ **Global state** - Can become hard to track",
            "lineNumber": 758
          },
          {
            "text": "- ❌ **Hard to test** - Must mock container or clear services",
            "lineNumber": 759
          },
          {
            "text": "- ❌ **Magic strings** - Service names are strings (typos)",
            "lineNumber": 760
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.39134109020233154
    },

registration\nservices.register('transitionManager', new TransitionManager({\n  preloadAll: true,\n}));\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Real-World Scenarios\n\n### Scenario 1: Simple App (Your Current Size)\n\n**Best: Direct Creation in App.js**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    this.registry = new Registry();\n    this.transitionManager = new TransitionManager({ registry:         "contents": "**Services needing configuration:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// SmoothScroll - might need different config in dev vs prod\nexport class SmoothScroll {\n  constructor(config = {}) {\n    this.lenis = new Lenis({\n      autoRaf: config.autoRaf ?? true,\n      duration: config.duration ?? 1.2,\n      // ... configurable options\n    });\n  }\n}\n\n// ❌ BAD: Hard-coded configuration\nconst scroll = new SmoothScroll(); // Uses defaults always\n\n// ✅ GOOD: Configure per environment\nconst scroll = new SmoothScroll({\n  duration: isDev ? 0.5 : 1.2,\n  autoRaf: !isSSR,\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Testability:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ❌ BAD: Hard to test\nclass Page {\n  constructor() {\n    this.transitionManager = new TransitionManager();\n    // Can't mock this!\n  }\n}\n\n// ✅ GOOD: Can inject mock\nclass Page {\n  constructor({ transitionManager }) {\n    this.transitionManager = transitionManager;\n  }\n}\n\n// In tests:\nconst mockTM = { getTransition: jest.fn() };\nconst page = new Page({ transitionManager: mockTM });\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Hybrid Approach: Best of Both Worlds\n\nYou don't need to choose one or the other! Use **both strategically**:\n\n### Strategy 1: Import Utilities, Inject Services\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ✅ Import pure utilities\nimport { $, $$ } from '../utils/Helpers.js';\nimport { Animation } from './Animation.js';\n\n// ✅ Inject stateful services\nexport default class Page {\n  constructor({ \n    // Injected services (stateful, configurable)\n    transitionManager,\n    smoothScroll,\n    // Imported utilities (pure, stateless)\n  }) {\n    this.transitionManager = transitionManager;\n    this.smoothScroll = smoothScroll;\n    \n    // Utilities can be imported and instantiated\n    this.animation = new Animation(); // ✅ Stateless, fine to create\n  }\n  \n  async create() {\n    // Use imported utilities\n    this.element = $(this.selector); // ✅ From import\n    \n    // Use injected services\n    await this.transitionManager.getTransition(route); // ✅ Injected\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Strategy 2: Factory Functions (Simplicity)",

        "contents": "- **Inheritance**: Classes extending other classes\n- **DI**: A technique to achieve composition\n\nDI helps with composition, but composition ≠ DI.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Inheritance (what you have)\nclass Home extends Page {\n  // Inherits all Page behavior\n}\n\n// Composition (alternative)\nclass Home {\n  constructor(pageBehavior) {\n    this.pageBehavior = pageBehavior; // Composed behavior\n  }\n}\n\n// DI helps composition\nclass Home {\n  constructor({ pageBehavior, animations, scroll }) {\n    // Compose multiple behaviors\n    this.behaviors = { pageBehavior, animations, scroll };\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**For your codebase:**\n- Keep inheritance for &#96;Home extends Page&#96; (it's fine!)\n- Use DI to compose services (&#96;transitionManager&#96;, &#96;smoothScroll&#96;)\n- They work together!\n\n---\n\n## Recommended Structure (Without Over-Engineering)\n\nYou don't need a huge Init.js! Here's a simple approach:\n\n### Option 1: App Creates Services (Simplest)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// App.js\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    // Create shared services in one place\n    this.registry = new Registry();\n    this.transitionManager = new TransitionManager({ registry: this.registry });\n    this.router = new Router({ registry: this.registry });\n    \n    // Create pages and inject\n    this.currentPage = new PageClass({\n      transitionManager: this.transitionManager,\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Option 2: Services Module (Clean Separation)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// services/index.js\nexport function createServices(config = {}) {\n  const registry = new Registry();\n  const transitionManager = new TransitionManager({ \n    registry,\n    ...config.transition \n  });\n  const router = new Router({ registry, ...config.router });\n  \n  return { registry, transitionManager, router };\n}\n\n// App.js\nimport { createServices } from './services/ServicesFactory.js';\n\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    this.services = createServices({\n      transition: { preloadAll: true },\n    });\n    \n    this.currentPage = new PageClass({\n      transitionManager: this.services.transitionManager,\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

        "contents": "this.elements = null;           // ✅ DOM element references\nthis.elements.page = null;      // ✅ DOM element reference\nthis.footnotes = null;          // ✅ NodeList (in Footnotes instance)\nthis.superscripts = null;       // ✅ NodeList (in Footnotes instance)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThese are **per-page state** that gets cleaned up even though the instance persists.\n\n### ❌ **Will NOT be GC'd** (Shared instance):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ServicesFactory.js\nconst footnotes = new Footnotes(); // ❌ Instance persists\n\n// App.js\nthis.footnotes = footnotes; // ❌ Reference persists\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe **Footnotes class instance** itself lives as long as the app runs.\n\n## Architectural Consideration\n\n### Current Pattern: **Singleton Service**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ✅ Works for stateless or global services\nconst smoothScroll = new SmoothScroll(); // Global scroll controller\nconst router = new Router(); // Global router\n\n// ⚠️ Questionable for page-specific services\nconst footnotes = new Footnotes(); // But has per-page DOM listeners\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Alternative Pattern: **Per-Page Instance**\n\nIf Footnotes manages **page-specific state** (DOM listeners, NodeLists), consider creating it per-page:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ServicesFactory.js\nexport function createServices() {\n  // Don't create footnotes here\n  return { registry, router, smoothScroll, transitionManager };\n}\n\n// Page.js\ncreate() {\n  // Create per-page instance\n  this.footnotes = new Footnotes({ smoothScroll: this.smoothScroll });\n  this.footnotes.init();\n}\n\ndestroy() {\n  this.footnotes.destroy(); // Properly cleanup\n  this.footnotes = null; // ✅ Now THIS instance can be GC'd\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Pros**:\n- ✅ Each page gets its own Footnotes instance\n- ✅ Instance can be fully GC'd when page is destroyed\n- ✅ No risk of cross-page listener conflicts\n\n**Cons**:\n- ❌ Creates new instance per page (small memory overhead)\n- ❌ Requires &#96;smoothScroll&#96; injection per page\n\n## Best Practice: Hybrid Approach\n\nFor shared services that manage per-page state:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Footnotes.js\nexport class Footnotes extends Component {\n  constructor({ smoothScroll }) {\n    super({ element: \".page-content aside\" });",

          },
          {
            "text": "const footnotes = new Footnotes(); // ❌ Instance persists",
            "lineNumber": 2193
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2194
          },
          {
            "text": "// App.js",
            "lineNumber": 2195
          },
          {
            "text": "this.footnotes = footnotes; // ❌ Reference persists",
            "lineNumber": 2196
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2197
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2198
          },
          {
            "text": "The **Footnotes class instance** itself lives as long as the app runs.",
            "lineNumber": 2199
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2200
          },
          {
            "text": "## Architectural Consideration",
            "lineNumber": 2201
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2202
          },
          {
            "text": "### Current Pattern: **Singleton Service**",
            "lineNumber": 2203
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2204
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;js",
            "lineNumber": 2205
          },
          {
            "text": "// ✅ Works for stateless or global services",
            "lineNumber": 2206
          },
          {
            "text": "const smoothScroll = new SmoothScroll(); // Global scroll controller",
            "lineNumber": 2207
          },
          {
            "text": "const router = new Router(); // Global router",
            "lineNumber": 2208
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2209
          },
          {
            "text": "// ⚠️ Questionable for page-specific services",
            "lineNumber": 2210
          },
          {
            "text": "const footnotes = new Footnotes(); // But has per-page DOM listeners",
            "lineNumber": 2211
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2212
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2213
          },
          {
            "text": "### Alternative Pattern: **Per-Page Instance**",
            "lineNumber": 2214
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2215
          },
          {
            "text": "If Footnotes manages **page-specific state** (DOM listeners, NodeLists), consider creating it per-page:",
            "lineNumber": 2216
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2217
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;js",
            "lineNumber": 2218
          },
          {
            "text": "// ServicesFactory.js",
            "lineNumber": 2219
          },
          {
            "text": "export function createServices() {",
            "lineNumber": 2220
          },
          {
            "text": "  // Don't create footnotes here",
            "lineNumber": 2221
          },
          {
            "text": "  return { registry, router, smoothScroll, transitionManager };",
            "lineNumber": 2222
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 2223
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2224
          },
          {
            "text": "// Page.js",
            "lineNumber": 2225
          },
          {
            "text": "create() {",
            "lineNumber": 2226
          },
          {
            "text": "  // Create per-page instance",
            "lineNumber": 2227
          },
          {
            "text": "  this.footnotes = new Footnotes({ smoothScroll: this.smoothScroll });",
            "lineNumber": 2228
          },
          {
            "text": "  this.footnotes.init();",
            "lineNumber": 2229
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 2230
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2231
          },
          {
            "text": "destroy() {",
            "lineNumber": 2232
          },
          {
            "text": "  this.footnotes.destroy(); // Properly cleanup",
            "lineNumber": 2233
          },
          {
            "text": "  this.footnotes = null; // ✅ Now THIS instance can be GC'd",
            "lineNumber": 2234
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 2235
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 2236
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2237
          },
          {
            "text": "**Pros**:",
            "lineNumber": 2238
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ Each page gets its own Footnotes instance",
            "lineNumber": 2239
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ Instance can be fully GC'd when page is destroyed",
            "lineNumber": 2240
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ No risk of cross-page listener conflicts",
            "lineNumber": 2241
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2242
          },
          {
            "text": "**Cons**:",
            "lineNumber": 2243
          },
          {
            "text": "- ❌ Creates new instance per page (small memory overhead)",
            "lineNumber": 2244
          },
          {
            "text": "- ❌ Requires &#96;smoothScroll&#96; injection per page",
            "lineNumber": 2245
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2246
          },
          {
            "text": "## Best Practice: Hybrid Approach",
            "lineNumber": 2247
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2248
          },
          {
            "text": "For shared services that manage per-page state:",
            "lineNumber": 2249
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2250
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;js",
            "lineNumber": 2251
          },
          {
            "text": "// Footnotes.js",
            "lineNumber": 2252
          },
          {
            "text": "export class Footnotes extends Component {",
            "lineNumber": 2253
          },
          {
            "text": "  constructor({ smoothScroll }) {",
            "lineNumber": 2254
          },
          {
            "text": "    super({ element: \".page-content aside\" });",
            "lineNumber": 2255
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.34548941254615784
    },

        "contents": "  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Strategy 2: Factory Functions (Simplicity)\n\nInstead of a complex Init.js, use factory functions:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// services/ServicesFactory.js\nexport function createAppServices(config = {}) {\n  const transitionManager = new TransitionManager(config.transition);\n  const smoothScroll = new SmoothScroll(config.scroll);\n  const router = new Router(config.router);\n  \n  return {\n    transitionManager,\n    smoothScroll,\n    router,\n  };\n}\n\n// App.js\nimport { createServices } from './services/ServicesFactory.js';\n\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    // Create services once\n    this.services = createAppServices({\n      scroll: { duration: 1.2 },\n      transition: { preloadAll: true },\n    });\n    \n    // Inject into pages\n    this.currentPage = new PageClass({\n      transitionManager: this.services.transitionManager,\n      smoothScroll: this.services.smoothScroll,\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Strategy 3: Service Locator (Simpler Alternative)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// services/ServiceContainer.js\nclass ServiceContainer {\n  constructor() {\n    this.services = new Map();\n  }\n  \n  register(name, service) {\n    this.services.set(name, service);\n  }\n  \n  get(name) {\n    return this.services.get(name);\n  }\n}\n\nexport const services = new ServiceContainer();\n\n// Init.js (or App.js)\nimport { services } from './services/ServiceContainer.js';\nimport { TransitionManager } from './classes/TransitionManager.js';\n\nservices.register('transitionManager', new TransitionManager());\nservices.register('smoothScroll', new SmoothScroll());\n\n// Page.js",

        "contents": "# Dependency Injection vs ES6 Imports: A Practical Guide\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [TL;DR](#tldr)\n- [The Spectrum](#the-spectrum)\n- [ES6 Imports: When They Work Well](#es6-imports-when-they-work-well)\n  - [✅ Good Candidates for ES6 Imports](#-good-candidates-for-es6-imports)\n  - [❌ Problems with ES6 Imports for Stateful Services](#-problems-with-es6-imports-for-stateful-services)\n- [Dependency Injection: When It Helps](#dependency-injection-when-it-helps)\n  - [✅ Good Candidates for DI](#-good-candidates-for-di)\n- [Hybrid Approach: Best of Both Worlds](#hybrid-approach-best-of-both-worlds)\n  - [Strategy 1: Import Utilities, Inject Services](#strategy-1-import-utilities-inject-services)\n  - [Strategy 2: Factory Functions (Simplicity)](#strategy-2-factory-functions-simplicity)\n  - [Strategy 3: Service Locator (Simpler Alternative)](#strategy-3-service-locator-simpler-alternative)\n- [Practical Example: Your Codebase Refactored](#practical-example-your-codebase-refactored)\n  - [Current Problem](#current-problem)\n  - [Refactored with Hybrid Approach](#refactored-with-hybrid-approach)\n- [Pros and Cons Comparison](#pros-and-cons-comparison)\n  - [ES6 Imports](#es6-imports)\n  - [Dependency Injection](#dependency-injection)\n  - [Hybrid (Recommended)](#hybrid-recommended)\n- [Composition vs Inheritance](#composition-vs-inheritance)\n- [Recommended Structure (Without Over-Engineering)](#recommended-structure-without-over-engineering)\n  - [Option 1: App Creates Services (Simplest)](#option-1-app-creates-services-simplest)\n  - [Option 2: Services Module (Clean Separation)](#option-2-services-module-clean-separation)\n  - [Option 3: Service Locator (Most Flexible)](#option-3-service-locator-most-flexible)\n- [Decision Matrix](#decision-matrix)\n- [Conclusion](#conclusion)\n- [Service Factory vs Service Locator: Complete Comparison](#service-factory-vs-service-locator-complete-comparison)\n  - [Detailed Comparison](#detailed-comparison)\n  - [Real-World Scenarios](#real-world-scenarios)\n  - [Hybrid Approach (Best of Both)](#hybrid-approach-best-of-both)\n  - [Recommendation Matrix](#recommendation-matrix)\n  - [For Your Codebase](#for-your-codebase)\n  - [Summary Table](#summary-table)\n  - [Final Recommendation](#final-recommendation)\n\n---\n\n## TL;DR\n\n- **ES6 imports**: Great for **pure utilities**, **stateless helpers**, and **stable singletons**\n- **DI (Dependency Injection)**: Better for **stateful services**, **testability**, **configuration**, and **lifecycle management**\n- **Hybrid approach**: Use ES6 imports for utilities, DI for services\n\n## The Spectrum\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nPure Utilities ←────────────→ Stateful Services\n   (imports)                    (injection)\n\nHelpers, Constants         Router, RouterPageManager\nPure Functions             Components with lifecycle\nStateless Classes          Things needing config\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## ES6 Imports: When They Work Well\n\n### ✅ Good Candidates for ES6 Imports\n\n**Pure utilities that don't need configuration:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// utils/Helpers.js\nexport function $(selector) {\n  return document.querySelector(selector);\n}\n\nexport function $$(selector) {\n  return document.querySelectorAll(selector);\n}\n\n// Usage anywhere\nimport { $, $$ } from './utils/Helpers.js';\nconst el = $('.my-class'); // ✅ Works great!\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

          },
          {
            "text": "## ES6 Imports: When They Work Well",

        "contents": "- Defined transitions between states\n- State-specific behavior\n- More structure for complex flows\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Example state machine\nthis.state = 'idle'; // idle → loading → loaded → error\n\nif (this.state === 'loading') return; // Can't start if already loading\nif (this.state === 'loaded') return; // Already done\nthis.state = 'loading'; // Transition\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## When to upgrade to a state machine\n- More than two states\n- Complex transitions\n- State-specific behavior\n- Need to track history or validate transitions\n\nFor your preloader, a guard clause is sufficient. If you later need states like &#96;idle&#96;, &#96;loading&#96;, &#96;animating&#96;, &#96;completed&#96;, &#96;error&#96;, then consider a state machine.\n\n## Best practices\n1. Set the flag immediately to prevent race conditions\n2. Check the flag first (early return)\n3. Use descriptive names (&#96;animationStarted&#96;, &#96;isInitialized&#96;, &#96;hasLoaded&#96;)\n4. Reset the flag when appropriate (e.g., in &#96;destroy()&#96;)\n\nYour implementation follows these practices.\n\n\n\n# Naming Conventions\n\n\n\n## Decision Tree for Naming\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nWhat does the function do?\n│\n├─ Creates and returns instances?\n│  └─ → Use \"create*\" ✅\n│\n├─ Configures/prepares (one-time)?\n│  └─ → Use \"setup*\" ✅\n│\n├─ Starts lifecycle after creation?\n│  └─ → Use \"init*\" ✅\n│\n└─ Retrieves existing instance?\n   └─ → Use \"get*\" ✅\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\n\n### Recommended Pattern\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// 1. CREATE - Instances\ncreateServices(config)  // ✅ Creates service instances\ncreateApp()             // ✅ Creates app instance\ncreatePage(id)          // ✅ Creates page instance\n\n// 2. SETUP - Configuration\nsetupHelpers()          // ✅ Configures DOM helpers\nsetupPageConfig()       // ✅ Returns config\nsetupRoutes()           // ✅ Configures routes\n\n// 3. INIT - Lifecycle\ninit()                  // ✅ Start app lifecycle\ninitRouter()            // ✅ Initialize router\ninitServices()          // ✅ Start service lifecycle\n\n// 4. GET - Retrieve",

        "contents": "#### 20. Implement Command Pattern for Navigation Actions\n**Issue:** Navigation flow is hard to test and undo\n**Solution:** Use Command pattern:avascript\nclass NavigationCommand {\n  constructor(router, href) {\n    this.router = router;\n    this.href = href;\n    this.previousState = null;\n  }\n  \n  async execute() {\n    this.previousState = this.router.saveState();\n    await this.router.performNavigation(this.href);\n  }\n  \n  async undo() {\n    if (this.previousState) {\n      await this.router.restoreState(this.previousState);\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n#### 21. Extract Page Factory Pattern\n**Issue:** Page creation logic is scattered across PageLoader\n**Solution:** Create PageFactory:pt\nclass PageFactory {\n  constructor(dependencies) {\n    this.dependencies = dependencies;\n  }\n  \n  async createPage(template, options = {}) {\n    const PageClass = await this.loadPageClass(template);\n    const page = new PageClass({\n      element: options.element || &#96;main[data-template=\"${template}\"]&#96;,\n      ...this.dependencies,\n      ...options\n    });\n    \n    if (options.autoCreate) {\n      await page.create();\n    }\n    \n    return page;\n  }\n}\n\n#### 22. Implement Event-Driven Architecture\n**Issue:** Components are tightly coupled\n**Solution:** Use event bus for communication:pt\nclass EventBus {\n  constructor() {\n    this.listeners = new Map();\n  }\n  \n  on(event, handler) {\n    if (!this.listeners.has(event)) {\n      this.listeners.set(event, []);\n    }\n    this.listeners.get(event).push(handler);\n  }\n  \n  emit(event, data) {\n    const handlers = this.listeners.get(event) || [];\n    handlers.forEach(handler =&gt; handler(data));\n  }\n}\n\n// Usage:\neventBus.emit('page:before-hide', { page, route });\neventBus.emit('page:after-show', { page });---\n\n## Design Pattern &amp; Architecture Suggestions\n\n### Current Architecture Analysis\n\nThe current architecture follows a **Service Layer Pattern** with clear separation of concerns:\n- **RouterRefactor**: Orchestrates navigation flow\n- **PageLoader**: Handles page class loading and instantiation\n- **PageRegistry**: Manages page instances and classes",

        "contents": "const el = $('.my-class'); // ✅ Works great!\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Constants and configuration:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// constants/Colors.js\nexport const RED = '#ff0000';\nexport const BLUE = '#0000ff';\n\n// Usage\nimport { RED, BLUE } from './constants/Colors.js'; // ✅ Fine to import\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Stateless classes:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// classes/Animation.js\nexport class Animation {\n  // Pure utility methods, no state\n  GSAPShowTransition(element) { /* ... */ }\n  GSAPHideTransition(element) { /* ... */ }\n}\n\n// Usage\nimport { Animation } from './classes/Animation.js';\nconst anim = new Animation();\n// ✅ No need to inject - it's stateless\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### ❌ Problems with ES6 Imports for Stateful Services\n\n**Your current code:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Page.js\nimport { TransitionManager } from \"./TransitionManager.js\";\n\nexport default class Page {\n  constructor() {\n    // ❌ Creates new instance every time\n    this.transitionManager = new TransitionManager();\n  }\n}\n\n// Every page creates its own TransitionManager\n// - Multiple instances doing the same work\n// - Can't share state/cache\n// - Hard to test (can't mock)\n// - Can't configure per environment\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**The issue:**\n- Each &#96;Page&#96; creates its own &#96;TransitionManager&#96;\n- Can't share preloaded images cache\n- Can't test with a mock &#96;TransitionManager&#96;\n- Hard-coded dependencies\n\n---\n\n## Dependency Injection: When It Helps\n\n### ✅ Good Candidates for DI\n\n**Stateful services with lifecycle:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// TransitionManager - maintains cache, has lifecycle\nexport class TransitionManager {\n  constructor() {\n    this.preloadedImages = new Map();           },
          {
            "lineNumber": 110
          },
          {
            "text": "**Your current code:**",

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "// Page.js",

          },
          {
            "text": "import { TransitionManager } from \"./TransitionManager.js\";",
            "lineNumber": 114
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 115
          },
          {
            "text": "export default class Page {",

          },
          {

          },

          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 120
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 121
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 122
          },
          {
            "text": "// Every page creates its own TransitionManager",

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "// - Can't share state/cache",

          },
          {
            "text": "// - Hard to test (can't mock)",
            "lineNumber": 126
          },
          {
            "text": "// - Can't configure per environment",

          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 128
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 129
          },
          {
            "text": "**The issue:**",

          },
          {
            "text": "- Each &#96;Page&#96; creates its own &#96;TransitionManager&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 131
          },
          {
            "text": "- Can't share preloaded images cache",
            "lineNumber": 132
          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "- Hard-coded dependencies",

          {
            "lineNumber": 135
          },

            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 136
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 137
          },
          {
            "text": "## Dependency Injection: When It Helps",
            "lineNumber": 138
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 139
          },

          },

          },

          },

            "lineNumber": 153
          },
          {

          {

GET - Retrieve\ngetServices()           // ✅ Get existing services\ngetRouter()            // ✅ Get existing router\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Common Confusion Points\n\n## The Semantic Difference\n\nNaming conventions should communicate **intent** and **what the function does**. Here's the standard meaning:\n\n| Name | Purpose | Returns | When to Use |\n|------|---------|---------|-------------|\n| **create** | Instantiate new instances | Object/Instance | Creating stateful objects |\n| **setup** | Configure/prepare (one-time) | void/undefined | Configuration, registration |\n| **init** | Initialize/start lifecycle | void/undefined | Starting after creation/setup |\n| **get** | Retrieve existing | Instance/Object | Accessing created instance |\n\n\n### Confusion 1: \"setupServices\" vs \"createServices\"\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ❌ CONFUSING: What does setupServices return?\nfunction setupServices() {\n  // Creates instances? Configures? Registers?\n}\n\n// ✅ CLEAR: Creates and returns services\nfunction createServices() {\n  return { router, registry };\n}\n\n// ✅ ALTERNATIVE: Setup registers (no return)\nfunction setupServices(container) {\n  container.register('router', new Router());\n  // No return - just registration\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Confusion 2: \"init\" vs \"create\" vs \"setup\"\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ❌ CONFUSING: What's the difference?\ncreateApp()\nsetupApp()\ninitApp()\n\n// ✅ CLEAR: Each has distinct purpose\nconst app = createApp(); // Creates instance\nsetupApp(app);           // Configures app\napp.init();              // Starts app lifecycle\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\n---\n\n## Summary\n\n| Function Name | Expectation | Returns | Example |\n|---------------|-------------|---------|---------|\n| &#96;create*&#96; | Creates new instances | Object/Instance | &#96;createServices()&#96; |\n| &#96;setup*&#96; | Configures/prepares | void or Config | &#96;setupHelpers()&#96; |\n| &#96;init*&#96; | Starts lifecycle | void | &#96;init()&#96; |\n| &#96;get*&#96; | Retrieves existing | Instance/Object | &#96;getServices()&#96; |\n\n**Your current naming:**\n- ✅ &#96;createServices()&#96; - Correct! Creates and returns\n- ✅ &#96;setupHelpers()&#96; - Correct! Configures (no return)\n- ✅ &#96;setupPageConfig()&#96; - Correct! Returns config\n\n**Consistency rule:**\n- **create** = Stateful instances (returns something)\n- **setup** = Configuration (usually void, sometimes config)\n- **init** = Lifecycle start (after creation)\n\nThis makes code self-documenting!\n\n# Dry Utilities\n\n\n---\n\n## Benefits Summary",

        "contents": "- **Inheritance**: Classes extending other classes\n- **DI**: A technique to achieve composition\n\nDI helps with composition, but composition ≠ DI.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Inheritance (what you have)\nclass Home extends Page {\n  // Inherits all Page behavior\n}\n\n// Composition (alternative)\nclass Home {\n  constructor(pageBehavior) {\n    this.pageBehavior = pageBehavior; // Composed behavior\n  }\n}\n\n// DI helps composition\nclass Home {\n  constructor({ pageBehavior, animations, scroll }) {\n    // Compose multiple behaviors\n    this.behaviors = { pageBehavior, animations, scroll };\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**For your codebase:**\n- Keep inheritance for &#96;Home extends Page&#96; (it's fine!)\n- Use DI to compose services (&#96;transitionManager&#96;, &#96;smoothScroll&#96;)\n- They work together!\n\n---\n\n## Recommended Structure (Without Over-Engineering)\n\nYou don't need a huge Init.js! Here's a simple approach:\n\n### Option 1: App Creates Services (Simplest)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// App.js\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    // Create shared services in one place\n    this.registry = new Registry();\n    this.transitionManager = new TransitionManager({ registry: this.registry });\n    this.router = new Router({ registry: this.registry });\n    \n    // Create pages and inject\n    this.currentPage = new PageClass({\n      transitionManager: this.transitionManager,\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Option 2: Services Module (Clean Separation)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// services/index.js\nexport function createServices(config = {}) {\n  const registry = new Registry();\n  const transitionManager = new TransitionManager({ \n    registry,\n    ...config.transition \n  });\n  const router = new Router({ registry, ...config.router });\n  \n  return { registry, transitionManager, router };\n}\n\n// App.js\nimport { createServices } from './services/ServicesFactory.js';\n\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    this.services = createServices({\n      transition: { preloadAll: true },\n    });\n    \n    this.currentPage = new PageClass({\n      transitionManager: this.services.transitionManager,\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

        "contents": "  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Strategy 2: Factory Functions (Simplicity)\n\nInstead of a complex Init.js, use factory functions:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// services/ServicesFactory.js\nexport function createAppServices(config = {}) {\n  const transitionManager = new TransitionManager(config.transition);\n  const smoothScroll = new SmoothScroll(config.scroll);\n  const router = new Router(config.router);\n  \n  return {\n    transitionManager,\n    smoothScroll,\n    router,\n  };\n}\n\n// App.js\nimport { createServices } from './services/ServicesFactory.js';\n\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    // Create services once\n    this.services = createAppServices({\n      scroll: { duration: 1.2 },\n      transition: { preloadAll: true },\n    });\n    \n    // Inject into pages\n    this.currentPage = new PageClass({\n      transitionManager: this.services.transitionManager,\n      smoothScroll: this.services.smoothScroll,\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Strategy 3: Service Locator (Simpler Alternative)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// services/ServiceContainer.js\nclass ServiceContainer {\n  constructor() {\n    this.services = new Map();\n  }\n  \n  register(name, service) {\n    this.services.set(name, service);\n  }\n  \n  get(name) {\n    return this.services.get(name);\n  }\n}\n\nexport const services = new ServiceContainer();\n\n// Init.js (or App.js)\nimport { services } from './services/ServiceContainer.js';\nimport { TransitionManager } from './classes/TransitionManager.js';\n\nservices.register('transitionManager', new TransitionManager());\nservices.register('smoothScroll', new SmoothScroll());\n\n// Page.js",

        "contents": "    this.currentPage = new PageClass({\n      transitionManager: this.services.transitionManager,\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Option 3: Service Locator (Most Flexible)\n\nSee Strategy 3 above - useful if services are needed in many places.\n\n---\n\n## Decision Matrix\n\n| Type | ES6 Import | DI |\n|------|-----------|-----|\n| Pure function | ✅ | ❌ |\n| Utility class (stateless) | ✅ | ❌ |\n| Constants | ✅ | ❌ |\n| Stateful service | ❌ | ✅ |\n| Needs configuration | ❌ | ✅ |\n| Needs to be shared | ❌ | ✅ |\n| Needs testing/mocking | ❌ | ✅ |\n\n---\n\n## Conclusion\n\n**For your codebase:**\n\n1. **Keep ES6 imports for:**\n   - &#96;Helpers.js&#96; utilities\n   - &#96;Animation.js&#96; (stateless)\n   - &#96;Colors.js&#96; constants\n\n2. **Use DI for:**\n   - &#96;TransitionManager&#96; (shared cache)\n   - &#96;Router&#96; (shared registry)\n   - &#96;SmoothScroll&#96; (might want per-page or shared)\n   - &#96;Registry&#96; (should be singleton)\n\n3. **Simple approach:**\n   - Create services in &#96;App.js&#96; constructor\n   - Pass to pages via constructor\n   - No need for complex Init.js unless you grow\n\n4. **Inheritance + DI:**\n   - Keep &#96;Home extends Page&#96; (inheritance is fine!)\n   - Inject services into &#96;Page&#96; (composition)\n   - They complement each other!\n\n\n# Service Factory vs Service Locator: Complete Comparison\n\n## Quick Decision Tree\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nNeed services in many places?\n├─ YES → Service Locator ✅\n└─ NO\n   │\n   Need complex initialization?\n   ├─ YES → Service Factory ✅\n   └─ NO → Direct creation in App.js ✅\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Comparison Table\n\n| Aspect | Service Factory | Service Locator | Direct Creation (App.js) |\n|--------|----------------|-----------------|--------------------------|\n| **Complexity** | Medium | Medium | Low ✅ |",

          {
            "text": "## Conclusion",
            "lineNumber": 583
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 584
          },
          {
            "text": "**For your codebase:**",
            "lineNumber": 585
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 586
          },
          {
            "text": "1. **Keep ES6 imports for:**",
            "lineNumber": 587
          },
          {
            "text": "   - &#96;Helpers.js&#96; utilities",
            "lineNumber": 588
          },
          {
            "text": "   - &#96;Animation.js&#96; (stateless)",
            "lineNumber": 589
          },
          {
            "text": "   - &#96;Colors.js&#96; constants",
            "lineNumber": 590
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 591
          },
          {
            "text": "2. **Use DI for:**",
            "lineNumber": 592
          },
          {
            "text": "   - &#96;TransitionManager&#96; (shared cache)",
            "lineNumber": 593
          },
          {
            "text": "   - &#96;Router&#96; (shared registry)",
            "lineNumber": 594
          },
          {
            "text": "   - &#96;SmoothScroll&#96; (might want per-page or shared)",
            "lineNumber": 595
          },
          {
            "text": "   - &#96;Registry&#96; (should be singleton)",
            "lineNumber": 596
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 597
          },
          {
            "text": "3. **Simple approach:**",
            "lineNumber": 598
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Create services in &#96;App.js&#96; constructor",
            "lineNumber": 599
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Pass to pages via constructor",
            "lineNumber": 600
          },
          {
            "text": "   - No need for complex Init.js unless you grow",
            "lineNumber": 601
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 602
          },
          {
            "text": "4. **Inheritance + DI:**",
            "lineNumber": 603
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Keep &#96;Home extends Page&#96; (inheritance is fine!)",
            "lineNumber": 604
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Inject services into &#96;Page&#96; (composition)",
            "lineNumber": 605
          },
          {
            "text": "   - They complement each other!",
            "lineNumber": 606
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 607
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 608
          },
          {
            "text": "# Service Factory vs Service Locator: Complete Comparison",
            "lineNumber": 609
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 610
          },
          {
            "text": "## Quick Decision Tree",
            "lineNumber": 611
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 612
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 613
          },
          {
            "text": "Need services in many places?",
            "lineNumber": 614
          },
          {
            "text": "├─ YES → Service Locator ✅",

          },
          {
            "text": "└─ NO",

          },
          {
            "text": "   │",
            "lineNumber": 617
          },
          {
            "text": "   Need complex initialization?",
            "lineNumber": 618
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 619
          },
          {
            "text": "   └─ NO → Direct creation in App.js ✅",
            "lineNumber": 620
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 622

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "## Comparison Table",
            "lineNumber": 625
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 626
          },
          {
            "text": "| Aspect | Service Factory | Service Locator | Direct Creation (App.js) |",
            "lineNumber": 627
          },
          {
            "text": "|--------|----------------|-----------------|--------------------------|",
            "lineNumber": 628
          },
          {

        "contents": "- Less likely to introduce bugs\n\n\n\n# Functions should return what it creates and computes\n\n## 1. **Return Values Pattern** / **Return What You Create**\n\nA function should return what it creates or computes, not require the caller to look it up elsewhere. This is a common functional programming principle.\n\n## 2. **Avoiding Unnecessary Indirection**\n\nThe anti-pattern you were experiencing is sometimes called:\n- **Unnecessary Indirection** — requiring lookups through intermediaries\n- **Registry Lookup Anti-pattern** — storing and then retrieving from a registry\n- **Double Lookup Pattern** — creating → storing → retrieving\n\n## 3. **Law of Demeter (LoD)** / **Principle of Least Knowledge**\n\nAvoid chaining through intermediaries. Prefer direct returns so callers don’t need to know internal storage details.\n\n## 4. **Command-Query Separation (CQS)** with nuance\n\nSeparate commands (mutations) from queries. It’s fine for a command that creates something to also return that value, so long as the side effect (registry update) and the return value are clear.\n\n## 5. **Function Composition** / **Composability**\n\nReturning values makes functions easier to compose and chain.\n\n## 6. **Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)**\n\nA function that creates something should also provide it, rather than forcing a separate lookup.\n\n## Most accurate term:\n\n**\"Return Values Pattern\"** or **\"Return What You Create\"** — functions should return what they create/manipulate, reducing unnecessary indirection.\n\nThe anti-pattern is sometimes called **\"Unnecessary Indirection\"** or **\"Double Lookup Anti-pattern\"**.\n\nThis aligns with functional programming principles where functions return values rather than relying on side effects (though side effects like registry updates can still exist).\n\n\n\n# Code Changes\n\nThe code stores pages in the registry and then retrieves them, which is redundant. Here's a cleaner approach:\n\n## Recommendation: Return page instances directly\n\n**Current pattern (problematic):**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Function sets in registry\ninitializePage(pageTemplate) {\n  const page = new pageClass(...);\n  this.pageRegistry.setCurrentPage(page); // Store\n  // No return\n}\n\n// Caller has to retrieve\nawait this.pageLoader.initializePage(template);\nconst page = this.pageRegistry.getCurrentPage(); // Retrieve again\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Better pattern:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Function returns the instance\ninitializePage(pageTemplate) {\n  const pageClass = this.pageRegistry.getPage(pageTemplate);",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "- ❌ **Hard to test** - Must mock container or clear services\n- ❌ **Magic strings** - Service names are strings (typos)\n- ❌ **No compile-time checking** - Errors only at runtime\n- ❌ **Tight coupling** - Code depends on container\n\n---\n\n## Detailed Comparison\n\n### Dependency Visibility\n\n**Service Factory:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ✅ Explicit - can see dependencies\nclass Page {\n  constructor({ transitionManager, router }) {\n    // Clear what's needed\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Service Locator:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ❌ Implicit - hidden dependencies\nclass Page {\n  constructor() {\n    this.transitionManager = services.get('transitionManager');\n    // Can't tell what services are needed without reading code\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Testing\n\n**Service Factory:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ✅ Easy to create test services\nconst testServices = createServices({\n  transition: { preloadAll: false },\n  router: { mockMode: true },\n});\n\nconst page = new Page({ transitionManager: testServices.transitionManager });\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Service Locator:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ⚠️ Must mock container or clear services\nservices.clear(); // Clear all\nservices.register('transitionManager', mockTM);\nconst page = new Page(); // Uses mocked service\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Access Pattern\n\n**Service Factory:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ✅ Must pass through constructors\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    this.services = createServices();\n  }\n  \n  createPage() {\n    return new Page({ \n      transitionManager: this.services.transitionManager \n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Service Locator:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ✅ Access from anywhere\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    services.register('router', new Router());\n  }\n}\n\nclass Page {\n  constructor() {\n    // ✅ Can access directly\n    this.router = services.get('router');\n  }\n}\n\nclass DeepComponent {\n  // ✅ Can access even here, 5 levels deep\n  handleClick() {\n    services.get('router').updatePage('/home');\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Configuration\n\n**Service Factory:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ✅ Easy to configure\nconst services = createServices({\n  transition: { preloadAll: true },\n  router: { enableLogging: isDev },\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Service Locator:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js",

        "contents": "GSAP timeline animates element\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Key Components\n\n### Router (&#96;app/router/Router.js&#96;)\n- Handles navigation lifecycle\n- Delegates route validation to RouterResolver\n- Coordinates page hiding/showing\n- Manages browser history via RouterHistory\n\n### RouterPageLoader (&#96;app/router/RouterPageLoader.js&#96;)\n- Dynamically loads page classes\n- Caches loaded classes in RegistryService\n- Initializes page instances with dependencies\n- Handles first page load\n\n### RouterPageManager (&#96;app/router/RouterPageManager.js&#96;)\n- Fetches page HTML via fetch()\n- Updates DOM with new page content\n- Extracts page metadata (template, background, color)\n- Preloads images before page display\n\n### RegistryService (&#96;app/services/RegistryService.js&#96;)\n- Registry of page classes (template → PageClass)\n- Tracks current page instance\n- Provides lookup methods\n\n### RouterResolver (&#96;app/router/RouterResolver.js&#96;)\n- Validates routes against SiteConfig\n- Normalizes route formats\n- Handles invalid routes (redirects, external links)\n- Returns RouteValidationResult objects\n\n### RouterHistory (&#96;app/router/RouterHistory.js&#96;)\n- Manages browser history state\n- Handles popstate events (back/forward)\n- Normalizes routes for history\n- Prevents duplicate history entries\n\n### AnimationsService (&#96;app/services/AnimationsService.js&#96;)\n- Discovers animations via data-animation attributes\n- Creates animation instances from registry\n- Manages shared IntersectionObserver\n- Cleans up animations on page destroy\n\n### TransitionsService (&#96;app/services/TransitionsService.js&#96;)\n- Manages page transition overlays\n- Preloads transition images\n- Updates transition templates from SiteConfig\n- Coordinates transition animations\n\n### SiteConfig (&#96;app/config/SiteConfig.js&#96;)\n- Central configuration for all routes\n- Maps templates to classes, URLs, and transitions\n- Single source of truth for route data\n\n### Page Base Class (&#96;app/pages/Page.js&#96;)\n- Base class for all pages\n- Implements lifecycle methods\n- Manages page elements and components\n- Handles page animations\n\n### Component Base Class (&#96;app/components/Component.js&#96;)\n- Base class for all components\n- Provides event management",

        "contents": "- Current page template\n\n**Usage:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Register a page class\nregistryService.setPage('home', Home);\n\n// Get a page class\nconst HomeClass = registryService.getPage('home');\n\n// Track current page\nregistryService.setCurrentPage(pageInstance);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3. Manager Pattern\nMultiple managers coordinate specific domains:\n\n- **RouterPageManager** (&#96;app/router/RouterPageManager.js&#96;): Manages page content updates, DOM manipulation, and page metadata\n- **AnimationsService** (&#96;app/services/AnimationsService.js&#96;): Manages page animations lifecycle, IntersectionObserver setup, and animation cleanup\n- **TransitionsService** (&#96;app/services/TransitionsService.js&#96;): Manages page transition overlays, image preloading, and transition templates\n\n### 4. Component Base Class Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/components/Component.js&#96;\n\nAll components inherit from a base &#96;Component&#96; class that provides:\n- Event management (via EventManager)\n- Element selection and caching\n- Lifecycle hooks (create, destroy)\n- Event emission/listening\n\n**Example:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nclass Preloader extends Component {\n  constructor() {\n    super({\n      element: SELECTORS.PRELOADER,\n      elements: { /* child selectors */ }\n    });\n  }\n  \n  create() {\n    super.create(); // Sets up this.element and this.elements\n    // Component-specific initialization\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 5. Lifecycle Hooks Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/pages/Page.js&#96;\n\nPages implement a clear lifecycle with optional hooks:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nclass Page {\n  async create() {\n    await this.beforeCreate?.()  // Optional hook\n    await this.createElements();\n    await this.createComponents();\n    this.createPageAnimations();\n    this.createPage();\n    await this.afterCreate?.()   // Optional hook\n  }\n  \n  async show() {\n    await this.beforeShow?.()\n    // Show logic\n    await this.afterShow?.()\n  }\n  \n  async hide(route) {\n    await this.beforeHide?.()\n    // Hide logic\n    await this.afterHide?.()\n  }\n  \n  async destroy() {\n    await this.beforeDestroy?.()\n    // Cleanup logic\n    await this.afterDestroy?.()\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 6. Orchestrator Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/services/Router.js&#96;\n\nThe &#96;Router&#96; orchestrates the page navigation lifecycle:\n\n1. **beforePageUpdate**: Validates route\n2. **startPageUpdate**: Hides current page, updates DOM, loads new page\n3. **afterPageUpdate**: Creates and shows new page\n\nThis pattern ensures a consistent, testable navigation flow.",

      "codeBlock": {

        "contents": "## Hybrid Approach (Best of Both)\n\nYou can combine both patterns:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// services/ServicesFactory.js - Factory\nexport function createServices(config = {}) {\n  const registry = new Registry();\n  const transitionManager = new TransitionManager({ registry });\n  const router = new Router({ registry });\n  \n  return { registry, transitionManager, router };\n}\n\n// services/ServiceContainer.js - Locator\nexport const services = new ServiceContainer();\n\n// App.js - Use both\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    // Create with factory\n    const appServices = createServices();\n    \n    // Register in locator (for deep access)\n    services.register('router', appServices.router);\n    services.register('transitionManager', appServices.transitionManager);\n    \n    // Inject explicitly (for main components)\n    this.currentPage = new Page({\n      transitionManager: appServices.transitionManager,\n      router: appServices.router,\n    });\n  }\n}\n\n// Deep components use locator\nclass Footer {\n  handleLink(href) {\n    services.get('router').updatePage(href); // ✅ No prop drilling\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**When to use hybrid:**\n- Main components: Explicit injection (clear dependencies)\n- Deep components: Service locator (avoid prop drilling)\n- Best of both worlds!\n\n---\n\n## Recommendation Matrix\n\n| Your Situation | Recommended Pattern | Why |\n|----------------|---------------------|-----|\n| **Small app (&lt; 10 services)** | Direct creation in App.js | Simplest |\n| **Medium app (10-20 services)** | Service Factory | Organized, configurable |\n| **Large app (20+ services)** | Service Factory + Locator | Factory for creation, Locator for access |\n| **Deep component tree** | Service Locator (or Hybrid) | Avoid prop drilling |\n| **Plugin system** | Service Locator | Plugins need access |\n| **Heavy testing** | Service Factory | Easy to mock |\n| **Rapid development** | Service Locator | Fast access |\n| **Long-term maintenance** | Service Factory | Clear dependencies |\n\n---\n\n## For Your Codebase\n\n### Current State\n- Medium-sized app",
