            "lineNumber": 985
          },
          {
            "text": "class Footer {",
            "lineNumber": 986
          },
          {
            "text": "  handleLink(href) {",
            "lineNumber": 987
          },
          {
            "text": "    services.get('router').updatePage(href); // ✅ No prop drilling",
            "lineNumber": 988
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 989
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 990
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 991
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 992
          },
          {
            "text": "**When to use hybrid:**",
            "lineNumber": 993
          },
          {
            "text": "- Main components: Explicit injection (clear dependencies)",
            "lineNumber": 994
          },
          {
            "text": "- Deep components: Service locator (avoid prop drilling)",
            "lineNumber": 995
          },
          {
            "text": "- Best of both worlds!",
            "lineNumber": 996
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 997
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 998
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 999
          },
          {
            "text": "## Recommendation Matrix",
            "lineNumber": 1000
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1001
          },
          {
            "text": "| Your Situation | Recommended Pattern | Why |",
            "lineNumber": 1002
          },
          {
            "text": "|----------------|---------------------|-----|",
            "lineNumber": 1003
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Small app (&lt; 10 services)** | Direct creation in App.js | Simplest |",
            "lineNumber": 1004
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Medium app (10-20 services)** | Service Factory | Organized, configurable |",
            "lineNumber": 1005
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Large app (20+ services)** | Service Factory + Locator | Factory for creation, Locator for access |",
            "lineNumber": 1006
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Deep component tree** | Service Locator (or Hybrid) | Avoid prop drilling |",
            "lineNumber": 1007
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Plugin system** | Service Locator | Plugins need access |",
            "lineNumber": 1008
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Heavy testing** | Service Factory | Easy to mock |",
            "lineNumber": 1009
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Rapid development** | Service Locator | Fast access |",
            "lineNumber": 1010
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Long-term maintenance** | Service Factory | Clear dependencies |",
            "lineNumber": 1011
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1012
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 1013
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1014
          },
          {
            "text": "## For Your Codebase",
            "lineNumber": 1015
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 1016
          },
          {
            "text": "### Current State",
            "lineNumber": 1017
          },
          {
            "text": "- Medium-sized app",
            "lineNumber": 1018
          }
        ]

        "contents": "# Page Class Refactoring Implementation Plan\n\n## Overview\nRefactor the Page class using composition with manager classes and Strategy pattern for show/hide behaviors, making Page a Facade that coordinates these managers while maintaining backward compatibility.\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Manager Classes Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nPage (Facade - ~80-100 lines)\n├── PageStateManager (tracks _created, _destroyed, _eventListenersSetup)\n├── PageElementManager (handles DOM queries and element creation)\n├── PageComponentManager (handles component initialization)\n├── PageLifecycleManager (orchestrates lifecycle hooks)\n└── ShowStrategy / HideStrategy (pluggable show/hide behaviors)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Implementation Steps\n\n### Step 1: Create PageStateManager\n**File**: &#96;app/pages/managers/PageStateManager.js&#96; (NEW)\n\nTrack page state flags and validate state transitions.\n\n### Step 2: Create PageElementManager\n**File**: &#96;app/pages/managers/PageElementManager.js&#96; (NEW)\n\nHandle DOM element queries, creation, and cleanup.\n\n### Step 3: Create PageComponentManager\n**File**: &#96;app/pages/managers/PageComponentManager.js&#96; (NEW)\n\nInitialize and cleanup page components (footnotes, smoothScroll).\n\n### Step 4: Create PageLifecycleManager\n**File**: &#96;app/pages/managers/PageLifecycleManager.js&#96; (NEW)\n\nOrchestrate lifecycle hook execution (beforeCreate, afterCreate, etc.).\n\n### Step 5: Create ShowStrategy and HideStrategy\n**File**: &#96;app/pages/strategies/ShowStrategy.js&#96; (NEW)\n**File**: &#96;app/pages/strategies/HideStrategy.js&#96; (NEW)\n\nExtract show/hide logic into pluggable strategy classes.\n\n### Step 6: Refactor Page Class\n**File**: &#96;app/pages/Page.js&#96;\n\nRefactor to use managers and strategies as a Facade, maintaining backward compatibility.\n\n## Backward Compatibility\n\n- All public methods remain the same\n- Lifecycle hooks still work\n- Property access via getters\n- Subclasses work without changes",

        "contents": "&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// In siteRoutes.js\n'/my-section': {\n  template: \"my-section\",\n  class: \"View\",  // Use View class\n  link: \"/my-section\",\n  url: \"/pages/my-section.html\",\n  title: \"My Section\",\n  metaDescription: \"Description\",\n  // ... rest of config\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe &#96;View&#96; class handles all standard page functionality automatically.\n\n### Step 4: Generate Static HTML\n\nAfter creating your template, generate the static HTML:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nbun run build:html:dev\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis generates &#96;pages/my-new-page.html&#96; from your Nunjucks template.\n\n### Step 5: Test Your Page\n\n1. Start the development server: &#96;bun run dev&#96;\n2. Navigate to &#96;http://localhost:3000/my-new-page&#96;\n3. Verify:\n   - Page loads correctly\n   - Transitions work\n   - Animations trigger\n   - Images load\n   - Navigation links work\n\n## Page Registry Setup\n\nThe Page Registry automatically manages page classes. Here's how it works:\n\n### Automatic Registration\n\nPages are registered automatically when first loaded:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// RouterPageLoader.loadPage() automatically:\n1. Checks if page class is already in registry\n2. If not, dynamically imports the page class\n3. Stores it in RegistryService.pages Map\n4. Returns the class for instantiation\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Manual Registration (Advanced)\n\nYou can manually register pages if needed:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// In your code\nconst MyPageClass = await import('./pages/MyPage.js');\nregistryService.setPage('my-page', MyPageClass.default);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Checking Page Status\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Check if page is registered\nif (registryService.hasPage('my-page')) {\n  const PageClass = registryService.getPage('my-page');\n}\n\n// Get current page instance\nconst currentPage = registryService.getCurrentPage();\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Animation System\n\nThe animation system uses data attributes to automatically discover and animate elements.\n\n### Using Built-in Animations\n\n#### Title Animation\n\nAdd &#96;data-animation=\"title\"&#96; to any element:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;html\n&lt;h1 data-animation=\"title\"&gt;Animated Title&lt;/h1&gt;\n&lt;h2 data-animation=\"title\"&gt;Another Animated Title&lt;/h2&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

        "contents": "3. **afterPageUpdate**: Creates and shows new page\n\nThis pattern ensures a consistent, testable navigation flow.\n\n### 7. Strategy Pattern (Animation Registry)\n**Location:** &#96;app/animations/AnimationsManager.js&#96;\n\nThe &#96;AnimationsManager&#96; uses a registry pattern to map animation types to animation classes:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nthis.animationRegistry = {\n  title: Titles,\n  // Future: image: Images, parallax: Parallax\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis allows easy extension with new animation types without modifying core logic.\n\n## Class Hierarchy\n\n### Application Layer\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nApp\n├── ServicesFactory (creates all services)\n│   ├── SiteConfig\n│   ├── Router\n│   ├── RegistryService\n│   ├── RouterPageLoader\n│   ├── RouterPageManager\n│   ├── RouterHistory\n│   ├── RouterResolver\n│   ├── AnimationsService\n│   ├── TransitionsService\n│   ├── SmoothScroll\n│   └── Footnotes\n├── Preloader (Component)\n└── Navigation (Component)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Page Layer\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nPage (base class)\n├── Home\n├── Introduction\n├── View (generic class for sections)\n└── References\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Component Layer\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nComponent (base class)\n├── Preloader\n├── Navigation\n├── SmoothScroll\n└── Footnotes\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Animation Layer\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nAnimationsService\n├── Titles\n├── BackgroundColors\n└── PreloaderAnimation\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Data Flow\n\n### Page Navigation Flow\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nUser clicks link\n    ↓\nRouter.setupLinkListeners() (event delegation)\n    ↓",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

        "contents": "|--------|----------------|-----------------|--------------------------|\n| **Complexity** | Medium | Medium | Low ✅ |\n| **Boilerplate** | Medium | Medium | Low ✅ |\n| **Access Pattern** | Pass as params | Global container | Pass as params |\n| **Testability** | Excellent ✅ | Good | Good |\n| **Flexibility** | High ✅ | Very High ✅ | Low |\n| **Explicit Dependencies** | Very explicit ✅ | Implicit | Very explicit ✅ |\n| **Best For** | Organized setup | Many consumers | Simple apps |\n| **When Services Needed** | At creation time | Anywhere, anytime | At creation time |\n| **Dependency Tracking** | Easy (import graph) | Hard (hidden) | Easy (import graph) ✅ |\n\n---\n\n## Service Factory Pattern\n\n### What It Is\n\nA function that creates and wires up all services, returning an object of services.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// services/ServicesFactory.js\nexport function createServices(config = {}) {\n  const registry = new Registry();\n  const transitionManager = new TransitionManager({ registry });\n  const router = new Router({ registry });\n  \n  return {\n    registry,\n    transitionManager,\n    router,\n  };\n}\n\n// App.js\nimport { createServices } from './services/ServicesFactory.js';\n\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    this.services = createServices();\n    this.router = this.services.router;\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Use Cases\n\n| Use Case | Example | Why Factory? |\n|----------|---------|--------------|\n| **Complex initialization** | Services need setup, config, wiring | ✅ Factory handles complexity |\n| **Environment-specific config** | Dev vs Prod settings | ✅ Pass config to factory |\n| **Service dependencies** | Registry → TransitionManager → Router | ✅ Factory wires dependencies |\n| **Organized codebase** | Want services separate from app logic | ✅ Clean separation |\n| **Multiple environments** | SSR, testing, production | ✅ Easy to create test services |\n| **Service lifecycle** | Services need initialization order | ✅ Factory controls order |\n\n### Pros\n\n- ✅ **Explicit dependencies** - Clear what's injected\n- ✅ **Easy to test** - Create services with test config\n- ✅ **Organized** - Services creation in one place\n- ✅ **Configurable** - Pass config per environment\n- ✅ **Type-safe** - Can add TypeScript/JSDoc easily\n- ✅ **Testable** - Can create mock services easily\n- ✅ **Clear ownership** - Know where services are created\n\n### Cons\n\n- ❌ **Must pass services** - Need to thread through constructors\n- ❌ **Not available everywhere** - Must pass to where needed",

        "contents": "  router: { enableLogging: isDev },\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Service Locator:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ⚠️ Configuration happens at registration\nservices.register('transitionManager', new TransitionManager({\n  preloadAll: true,\n}));\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Real-World Scenarios\n\n### Scenario 1: Simple App (Your Current Size)\n\n**Best: Direct Creation in App.js**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    this.registry = new Registry();\n    this.transitionManager = new TransitionManager({ registry: this.registry });\n    this.router = new Router({ registry: this.registry });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Why:** Simplest, no extra complexity needed.\n\n### Scenario 2: Growing App with Many Services\n\n**Best: Service Factory**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    this.services = createServices({\n      transition: { preloadAll: true },\n      router: { enableAnalytics: true },\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Why:** Organized, configurable, clear separation.\n\n### Scenario 3: Deep Component Tree\n\n**Best: Service Locator (or Hybrid)**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Deep component needs router\nclass Footer extends Component {\n  handleLink(href) {\n    services.get('router').updatePage(href);\n    // ✅ No need to pass router through 5 component layers\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Why:** Avoids prop drilling.\n\n### Scenario 4: Testing\n\n**Best: Service Factory**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Easy to create test services\nconst Third-party plugin can access services\nclass MyPlugin {\n  init() {\n    const router = services.get('router');\n    router.addRoute('/my-route', handler);\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Why:**         "contents": "# Architecture Overview\n\n## Table of Contents\n- [Core Architecture](#core-architecture)\n- [Design Patterns](#design-patterns)\n- [Class Hierarchy](#class-hierarchy)\n- [Data Flow](#data-flow)\n- [Key Components](#key-components)\n\n## Core Architecture\n\nThis single-page application (SPA) is built with vanilla JavaScript, following a modular architecture that emphasizes separation of concerns, dependency injection, and a service-oriented design.\n\n### Entry Point\n\nThe application starts at &#96;app/App.js&#96;, which:\n1. Initializes the service factory to create all services\n2. Sets up the router to handle navigation\n3. Creates the preloader for initial page load\n4. Manages the application lifecycle\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// App.js structure\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    this.pageConfig = setupPageConfig();\n    this.preloaderVisible = false;\n  }\n\n  async init() {\n    this.createServices();\n    await this.transitionsService.init();\n    await this.services.router.start(); // Calls pageLoader.create() to initialize the first page\n    this.currentPage = this.services.registryService.getCurrentPage();\n    this.createNavigation();\n    this.createPreloader();\n    liveReload();\n  }\n\n  createServices() {\n    this.services = createServices();\n    this.siteConfig = this.services.siteConfig;\n    this.router = this.services.router;\n    this.navigation = this.services.navigation;\n    this.smoothScroll = this.services.smoothScroll;\n    this.animationsService = this.services.animationsService;\n    this.transitionsService = this.services.transitionsService;\n    this.footnotes = this.services.footnotes;\n    this.pageRegistry = this.services.registryService;\n    this.pageLoader = this.services.routerPageLoader;\n    this.pageManager = this.services.routerPageManager;\n    this.routerHistory = this.services.routerHistory;\n    this.routerResolver = this.services.routerResolver;\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

        "contents": "import { Preloader } from \"./components/Preloader.js\";\nimport { Navigation } from \"./components/Navigation.js\";\nimport { $, setupHelpers } from \"./utils/Helpers.js\";\nimport { liveReload, setupPageConfig } from \"./utils/Environment.js\";\n\nclass App {\n  /**\n   * Constructor: Configuration only (pure, no side effects)\n   */\n  constructor() {\n    // ✅ Configuration: Setup page config\n    this.pageConfig = setupPageConfig();\n    \n    // ✅ Configuration: Store references (no DOM lookup)\n    this.pageHistory = window.history;\n    \n    // ✅ Configuration: Initialize state containers\n    this.pages = new Map();\n    \n    // ✅ Configuration: Initialize flags\n    this._initialized = false;\n    \n    // ❌ NO side effects\n    // ❌ NO DOM access\n    // ❌ NO async operations\n  }\n  \n  /**\n   * Initialize application (side effects, DOM access, async)\n   * Call this after constructor\n   */\n  async init() {\n    if (this._initialized) {\n      console.warn('App.init() called multiple times');\n      return;\n    }\n    this._initialized = true;\n    \n    // 1. Setup helpers (modifies prototypes)\n    setupHelpers();\n    \n    // 2. Create services\n    this.createServices();\n    \n    // 3. Setup pages (async, DOM access)\n    await this.setupPages();\n    \n    // 4. Setup app event listeners\n    this.setupApp();\n    this.setupEventListeners();\n    \n    // 5. Create preloader\n    this.createPreloader();\n    \n    // 6. Enable hot reload\n    liveReload();\n  }\n  \n  /**\n   * Create the services for the application\n   */\n  createServices() {\n    this.services = createServices();\n    this.registry = this.services.registry;\n    this.router = this.services.router;\n    this.smoothScroll = this.services.smoothScroll;\n    this.transitionManager = this.services.transitionManager;\n  }\n  \n  /**\n   * Set up app event listeners and router\n   */\n  setupApp() {\n    // ✅ Guard DOM ready state",

        "contents": "- **PageLoader**: Handles page class loading and instantiation\n- **PageRegistry**: Manages page instances and classes\n- **PageManager**: Handles DOM updates\n- **RouterResolver**: Validates routes\n- **RouterHistory**: Manages browser history\n\n### Recommended Improvements\n\n#### 1. **Observer Pattern for Page Lifecycle Events**\n\nInstead of direct method calls, use events for lifecycle hooks:\nript\nclass PageLifecycleManager {\n  constructor(eventBus) {\n    this.eventBus = eventBus;\n  }\n  \n  async transitionPage(fromPage, toPage, route) {\n    this.eventBus.emit('page:before-hide', { page: fromPage, route });\n    await fromPage.hide(route);\n    this.eventBus.emit('page:after-hide', { page: fromPage });\n    \n    this.eventBus.emit('page:before-show', { page: toPage });\n    await toPage.show();\n    this.eventBus.emit('page:after-show', { page: toPage });\n  }\n}**Benefits:**\n- Decouples components\n- Easy to add logging, analytics, error tracking\n- Allows plugins/extensions\n- Better testability\n\n#### 2. **Pipeline Pattern for Navigation Flow**\n\nBreak navigation into a pipeline of steps:\nascript\nclass NavigationPipeline {\n  constructor() {\n    this.steps = [];\n  }\n  \n  addStep(step) {\n    this.steps.push(step);\n    return this;\n  }\n  \n  async execute(context) {\n    for (const step of this.steps) {\n      context = await step.execute(context);\n      if (context.shouldAbort) break;\n    }\n    return context;\n  }\n}\n\n// Usage:\nconst pipeline = new NavigationPipeline()\n  .addStep(new ValidateRouteStep())\n  .addStep(new HideCurrentPageStep())\n  .addStep(new UpdateDOMStep())\n  .addStep(new LoadPageClassStep())\n  .addStep(new ShowNewPageStep());\n\nawait pipeline.execute({ href, router: this });**Benefits:**\n- Easy to add/remove steps\n- Clear flow visualization\n- Can add middleware (logging, error handling)\n- Testable individual steps\n\n#### 3. **Repository Pattern for Page Storage**\n\nMake PageRegistry a true repository:\n\nclass PageRepository {\n  constructor() {\n    this.pageClasses = new Map(); // Page class definitions",

      "codeBlock": {

        "range": {

          "endPosition": {
            "line": 1070

        },
        "contents": "## For Your Codebase\n\n### Current State\n- Medium-sized app\n- Services: Registry, Router, TransitionManager, SmoothScroll\n- Some services shared, some per-page\n- Testing not yet heavy\n\n### Recommendation: **Service Factory** ✅\n\n**Why:**\n1. ✅ Organized - Clean separation of service creation\n2. ✅ Configurable - Can set dev vs prod settings\n3. ✅ Testable - Easy to create test services\n4. ✅ Explicit - Clear what services are needed\n5. ✅ Future-proof - Easy to add more services\n6. ✅ Not too complex - Simple factory function\n\n**Implementation:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// services/ServicesFactory.js\nexport function createServices(config = {}) {\n  const registry = new Registry();\n  const transitionManager = new TransitionManager({ \n    registry,\n    ...config.transition \n  });\n  const router = new Router({ \n    registry,\n    ...config.router \n  });\n  \n  return {\n    registry,\n    transitionManager,\n    router,\n  };\n}\n\n// App.js\nimport { createServices } from './services/ServicesFactory.js';\n\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    this.services = createServices({\n      transition: { preloadAll: true },\n    });\n    \n    // Inject into pages\n    this.currentPage = new PageClass({\n      transitionManager: this.services.transitionManager,\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

        "contents": "Make PageRegistry a true repository:\n\nclass PageRepository {\n  constructor() {\n    this.pageClasses = new Map(); // Page class definitions\n    this.pageInstances = new Map(); // Page instances by template\n  }\n  \n  async findPageClass(template) {\n    if (this.pageClasses.has(template)) {\n      return this.pageClasses.get(template);\n    }\n    return await this.loadPageClass(template);\n  }\n  \n  async findOrCreatePage(template, factory) {\n    if (this.pageInstances.has(template)) {\n      return this.pageInstances.get(template);\n    }\n    const page = await factory.create(template);\n    this.pageInstances.set(template, page);\n    return page;\n  }\n  \n  setCurrentPage(page) {\n    this.currentPage = page;\n    this.currentTemplate = page.template;\n  }\n}**Benefits:**\n- Clear data access layer\n- Can add caching strategies\n- Easy to swap implementations\n- Better separation of concerns\n\n#### 4. **Chain of Responsibility for Route Resolution**\n\nHandle different route types with chain:\n\nclass RouteHandler {\n  constructor(nextHandler = null) {\n    this.nextHandler = nextHandler;\n  }\n  \n  canHandle(href) {\n    return false;\n  }\n  \n  async handle(href, context) {\n    if (this.canHandle(href)) {\n      return this.process(href, context);\n    }\n    if (this.nextHandler) {\n      return this.nextHandler.handle(href, context);\n    }\n    throw new Error(&#96;No handler for route: ${href}&#96;);\n  }\n  \n  async process(href, context) {\n    throw new Error('Must implement process');\n  }\n}\n\nclass HomeRouteHandler extends RouteHandler {\n  canHandle(href) {\n    return href === '/' || href === '' || href === 'home';\n  }\n  \n  async process(href, context) {\n    return { route: 'home', normalizedPath: 'home' };\n  }\n}\n\nclass SectionRouteHandler extends RouteHandler {\n  canHandle(href) {\n    return href.startsWith('section-');\n  }\n  \n  async process(href, context) {\n    return { route: href, normalizedPath: href };\n  }\n}\n\n// Build chain\nconst routeHandler = new HomeRouteHandler(\n  new SectionRouteHandler(\n    new DefaultRouteHandler()\n  )\n);\n\n#### 5. **Modern Page Lifecycle Pattern**",

        "contents": "Router.setupLinkListeners() (event delegation)\n    ↓\nRouter.updatePage(href)\n    ↓\nRouter.beforePageUpdate(href)\n    ├── RouterResolver.validateRoute()\n    └── Returns RouteValidationResult\n    ↓\nRouter.startPageUpdate(routeInfo)\n    ├── CurrentPage.hide(route)\n    │   ├── TransitionsService.updateTransitionOverlay()\n    │   └── TransitionsService.showPageTransition()\n    ├── RouterPageManager.updatePage(route)\n    │   ├── Fetch HTML\n    │   ├── Update DOM\n    │   ├── Update page metadata\n    │   └── Preload images\n    ├── RouterHistory.updateHistory()\n    └── RouterPageLoader.getPage(route)\n        ├── Load page class (if not cached)\n        └── Initialize page instance\n    ↓\nRouter.afterPageUpdate(newPage, routeInfo)\n    ├── newPage.create()\n    │   ├── createElements()\n    │   ├── createComponents()\n    │   ├── createPageAnimations()\n    │   └── setupEventListeners()\n    └── newPage.show()\n        ├── TransitionsService.hidePageTransition()\n        └── SmoothScroll.scrollTo(0)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Page Lifecycle Flow\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nPage Creation:\ncreate() → beforeCreate → createElements → createComponents → \ncreatePageAnimations → createPage → afterCreate\n\nPage Display:\nshow() → beforeShow → hidePageTransition → scrollTo(0) → afterShow\n\nPage Hiding:\nhide(route) → beforeHide → updateTransitionOverlay → \nshowPageTransition → destroy() → afterHide\n\nPage Destruction:\ndestroy() → beforeDestroy → destroyPageAnimations → \nremoveEventListeners → destroyComponents → destroyElements → afterDestroy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Animation Flow\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nPage.create()\n    ↓\nPage.createPageAnimations()\n    ↓\nAnimationsService.createPageAnimations(pageElement)\n    ├── Find elements with [data-animation]\n    ├── Group by animation type\n    ├── Create animation instances\n    └── Setup shared IntersectionObserver\n    ↓\nIntersectionObserver detects viewport entry\n    ↓\nAnimation.animateIn() (e.g., Titles.animateIn())\n    ↓\nGSAP timeline animates element\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Key         "contents": "# Page Class Refactoring Strategy\n\n## Current State Analysis\n\nThe &#96;Page&#96; class ([app/pages/Page.js](app/pages/Page.js)) currently has **226 lines** and violates the Single Responsibility Principle by handling:\n\n1. **Lifecycle Management** - create, destroy, show, hide orchestration\n2. **DOM Element Management** - element queries, creation, cleanup\n3. **Component Coordination** - footnotes, smoothScroll initialization\n4. **Animation Coordination** - delegating to AnimationsManager\n5. **Transition Coordination** - delegating to TransitionsManager  \n6. **State Tracking** - &#96;_created&#96;, &#96;_destroyed&#96;, &#96;_eventListenersSetup&#96; flags\n7. **Event Management** - setup/removal of event listeners\n\n## Recommended Refactoring Approaches\n\n### Option 1: Composition with Manager Classes (Recommended)\n\nExtract responsibilities into focused manager classes that Page composes:\n\n#### Extract &#96;PageElementManager&#96;\n\n- Handles DOM queries and element creation\n- Methods: &#96;createElements()&#96;, &#96;destroyElements()&#96;\n- Manages: &#96;element&#96;, &#96;elements&#96;, &#96;pageTransition&#96;, &#96;preloader&#96;\n\n#### Extract &#96;PageComponentManager&#96;  \n\n- Handles component initialization and cleanup\n- Methods: &#96;createComponents()&#96;, &#96;destroyComponents()&#96;\n- Manages: &#96;footnotes&#96;, &#96;smoothScroll&#96; setup\n\n#### Extract &#96;PageLifecycleManager&#96;\n\n- Orchestrates lifecycle hooks and state transitions\n- Methods: &#96;executeCreate()&#96;, &#96;executeDestroy()&#96;, &#96;executeShow()&#96;, &#96;executeHide()&#96;\n- Manages: &#96;_created&#96;, &#96;_destroyed&#96; flags and hook execution order\n\n#### Extract &#96;PageStateManager&#96;\n\n- Tracks page state and prevents duplicate operations\n- Methods: &#96;isCreated()&#96;, &#96;isDestroyed()&#96;, &#96;markCreated()&#96;, &#96;markDestroyed()&#96;\n- Manages: state flags and validation\n\n**Result**: Page becomes a **Facade** that coordinates these managers, reducing from ~226 lines to ~80-100 lines.\n\n### Option 2: Strategy Pattern for Show/Hide Behaviors\n\nExtract show/hide logic into strategy classes:\n\n- &#96;DefaultShowStrategy&#96; - handles standard show behavior\n- &#96;DefaultHideStrategy&#96; - handles standard hide behavior\n- Subclasses can inject custom strategies",

        "contents": "- ✅ Direct access to parent methods\n- ✅ Good for \"IS-A\" relationships (Home IS-A Page)\n- ✅ Less boilerplate\n\n**Cons:**\n- ❌ Tight coupling - subclass depends on parent\n- ❌ Can't easily swap implementations\n- ❌ Single inheritance only (can't extend multiple classes)\n- ❌ Overriding can break parent logic\n- ❌ Hard to test in isolation\n\n### Composition (Alternative Approach)\n\n**Pros:**\n- ✅ Loose coupling - can swap behaviors\n- ✅ Flexible - mix and match behaviors\n- ✅ Testable - test behaviors independently\n- ✅ No inheritance hierarchy\n- ✅ Can use multiple behaviors simultaneously\n\n**Cons:**\n- ⚠️ More complex - more classes/interfaces\n- ⚠️ More boilerplate\n- ⚠️ Must pass dependencies through\n\n---\n\n## Could Composition Solve Your Issues?\n\n**Short answer: Yes, but it might be overkill for your use case.**\n\n### Current Problem with Inheritance\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Problem: Overriding requires duplication\nclass Home extends Page {\n  async show() {\n    // Must duplicate parent logic\n    super.show(); // Can't easily customize specific step\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### How Composition Would Solve It\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Composition approach\nclass Page {\n  constructor({ showBehavior, hideBehavior }) {\n    this.showBehavior = showBehavior;\n    this.hideBehavior = hideBehavior;\n  }\n  \n  async show() {\n    await this.showBehavior.execute(this);\n  }\n}\n\n// Easy to customize\nclass Home extends Page {\n  constructor() {\n    super({\n      showBehavior: new CustomShowBehavior(), // Swap behavior\n      hideBehavior: new DefaultHideBehavior(),\n    });\n  }\n}\n\n// Or use hooks with composition\nclass Page {\n  constructor({ hooks = {} }) {\n    this.hooks = hooks;\n  }\n  \n  async show() {\n    await this.hooks.onBeforeShow?.();\n    // ... base logic ...\n    await this.hooks.onAfterShow?.();\n  }\n}\n\nclass Home {\n  constructor() {\n    super({\n      hooks: {\n        onAfterShow: () =&gt; this.playWelcomeAnimation(),\n      },\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Recommendation for Your Codebase\n\n### For Your Current Size: Inheritance + Hooks ✅\n\n**Why:**\n- Simple codebase - don't need composition complexity",

});\n    \n    // ✅ 1.4: Store dependencies\n    this.service = options.service;\n    \n    // ✅ 1.5: Initialize flags\n    this._created = false;\n    this._destroyed = false;\n    this._listenersSetup = false;\n    \n    // ✅ 1.6: Initialize event tracking\n    this._eventHandlers = new Map();\n    \n    // ✅ 1.8: Initialize state\n    this.data = null;\n  }\n  \n  // return;\n    \n    // ✅ 2.2: Call super\n    super.create();\n    \n    // ✅ 2.3: Verify elements\n    if (!this.element) {\n      console.warn(\"Component element not found\");\n      return;\n    }\n    \n    // ✅ 2.4: Process data\n    this.processData();\n    \n    // ✅ 2.6: Set up listeners\n    this.setupEventListeners();\n    \n    // ✅ 2.8: Start operations\n    await this.initialize();\n    \n    // ✅ 2.9: Mark as created\n    this._created = true;\n  }\n  \n  setupEventListeners() {\n    // ✅ 2.6.1: Idempotent guard\n    if (this._listenersSetup) return;\n    \n         "contents": "  async onBeforeCreate() {} // Optional\n  async onAfterCreate() {} // Optional\n  async onBeforeShow() {} // Optional\n  async onAfterShow() {} // Optional\n  async onBeforeHide(route) {} // Optional\n  async onAfterHide(route) {} // Optional\n  onBeforeDestroy() {} // Optional\n  onAfterDestroy() {} // Optional\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Subclass Using Hooks\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Home.js\nexport class Home extends Page {\n  constructor() {\n    super({\n      id: \"home\",\n      element: \".home\",\n      elements: { /* ... */ },\n    });\n  }\n  \n  // ✅ Only define hooks you need\n  async onAfterCreate() {\n    // Custom logic after page is created\n    this.setupHomeSpecificFeatures();\n  }\n  \n  async onAfterShow() {\n    // Custom logic after page is shown\n    this.playWelcomeAnimation();\n    this.initializeHomeSlider();\n  }\n  \n  async onBeforeHide(route) {\n    // Custom cleanup before hiding\n    this.stopHomeAnimations();\n  }\n}\n\n// View.js - No hooks needed, uses parent implementation\nexport class View extends Page {\n  constructor({ id, element, elements }) {\n    super({ id, element, elements });\n  }\n  // ✅ Doesn't need to define anything - uses parent's show/hide\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Composition vs Inheritance\n\n### Current: Inheritance\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nclass Page {\n  async show() { /* ... */ }\n}\n\nclass Home extends Page {\n  // Home IS-A Page\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Alternative: Composition\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Page is a composition of behaviors\nclass Page {\n  constructor(behaviors = {}) {\n    this.showBehavior = behaviors.show || new DefaultShowBehavior();\n    this.hideBehavior = behaviors.hide || new DefaultHideBehavior();\n  }\n  \n  async show() {\n    await this.showBehavior.execute(this);\n  }\n}\n\n// Home uses composition\nclass Home {\n  constructor() {\n    super({\n      show: new HomeShowBehavior(), // Custom behavior\n      hide: new DefaultHideBehavior(), // Default behavior\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Inheritance vs Composition Comparison\n\n### Inheritance (Current Approach)\n\n**Pros:**\n- ✅ Simple - familiar pattern\n- ✅ Direct access to parent methods\n- ✅ Good for \"IS-A\" relationships (Home IS-A Page)\n- ✅ Less boilerplate\n\n**Cons:**\n- ❌ Tight coupling - subclass depends on parent",

        "contents": "### For Your Current Size: Inheritance + Hooks ✅\n\n**Why:**\n- Simple codebase - don't need composition complexity\n- Hooks solve the overriding problem\n- Familiar pattern (inheritance)\n- Easy to understand\n\n**Implementation:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Page.js - Add hooks\nasync show() {\n  // Base logic\n  if (!this.smoothScroll.enabled() &amp;&amp; !this.preloader) {\n    this.smoothScroll.create();\n    this.smoothScroll.scrollTo(0, {immediate: true});\n  }\n  \n  // ✅ Hook point\n  await this.onBeforeShow?.();\n  \n  await this.animation.GSAPHideTransition(this.transitionOverlay);\n  \n  // ✅ Hook point\n  await this.onAfterShow?.();\n}\n\n// Home.js - Use hooks\nexport class Home extends Page {\n  async onAfterShow() {\n    this.playWelcomeAnimation();\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### When to Consider Composition\n\nConsider composition if:\n- You have 10+ page types with very different behaviors\n- You need to swap behaviors at runtime\n- You need to test behaviors in isolation\n- You want maximum flexibility\n\nFor now, **inheritance + hooks** is the sweet spot.\n\n---\n\n## Summary\n\n**Subclasses:** Yes, classes like &#96;Home extends Page&#96; are subclasses.\n\n**Overriding problems:**\n- Code duplication\n- Fragile to parent changes\n- Hard to maintain\n\n**Hooks solution:**\n- Optional extension points\n- No duplication\n- Safe customization\n\n**Composition alternative:**\n- More flexible\n- More complex\n- Probably overkill for your size\n\n**Recommendation:** Use inheritance with hooks - best balance of simplicity and flexibility for your codebase.\n\n\n\n# Making Lifecycle Methods Idempotent\n\n## What Is Idempotency?\n\n**Idempotent** = Calling a method multiple times has the same effect as calling it once.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// ✅ Idempotent\ncreate(); // Creates page\ncreate(); // Does nothing (already created)\ncreate(); // Does nothing (already created)\n// Result: Page created once ✅\n\n// ❌ Not idempotent\ncreate(); // Creates page + attaches listeners\ncreate(); // Creates page AGAIN + attaches listeners AGAIN\n// Result: Duplicate listeners, animations, memory leaks ❌\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Why Idempotency Matters\n\nLifecycle methods (&#96;create()&#96;, &#96;destroy()&#96;) can be called multiple times in real-world scenarios:\n\n- **Rapid navigation**: User clicks links quickly before pages finish loading",

        "contents": "- ✅ Full control - can change any part\n- ✅ Simple concept - just override method\n- ✅ No framework needed - native JavaScript\n\n**Cons:**\n- ❌ Code duplication - must copy parent logic\n- ❌ Fragile - parent changes break subclasses\n- ❌ Maintenance burden - update multiple files\n- ❌ Easy to miss steps - forget important logic\n- ❌ Hard to test - more code to test\n\n### Hooks (Recommended Pattern)\n\n**Pros:**\n- ✅ No duplication - parent logic in one place\n- ✅ Robust - parent changes apply automatically\n- ✅ Clean - subclasses only add what's needed\n- ✅ Safe - can't break parent logic\n- ✅ Flexible - optional hooks, define what you need\n\n**Cons:**\n- ⚠️ Slightly more complex - need to design hook points\n- ⚠️ Must remember to call hooks in parent\n- ⚠️ Less control - can't change parent logic order\n\n---\n\n## Complete Hook Implementation\n\n### Parent Class with Hooks\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport default class Page {\n  constructor({ id, element, elements }) {\n    ",

        "contents": "### Current Situation (Good - No Overriding Yet)\n\nYour current subclasses don't override &#96;show()&#96; or &#96;hide()&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Page.js (parent)\nasync show() {\n  if (!this.smoothScroll.enabled() &amp;&amp; !this.preloader) {\n    this.smoothScroll.create();\n    this.smoothScroll.scrollTo(0, {immediate: true});\n  }\n  await this.animation.GSAPHideTransition(this.transitionOverlay);\n}\n\n// Home.js (subclass)\n// ✅ Doesn't override show() - uses parent's implementation\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Problem Scenario: When You Need to Customize\n\nWhat if &#96;Home&#96; page needs to do something extra when showing?\n\n**Option 1: Override Entire Method (❌ Bad)**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Home.js\nexport class Home extends Page {\n  async show() {\n    // ❌ PROBLEM: Must duplicate ALL parent logic\n    if (!this.smoothScroll.enabled() &amp;&amp; !this.preloader) {\n      this.smoothScroll.create();\n      this.smoothScroll.scrollTo(0, {immediate: true});\n    }\n    await this.animation.GSAPHideTransition(this.transitionOverlay);\n    \n    // ✅ Only this part is new (what we actually want to customize)\n    this.playWelcomeAnimation();\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Problems with overriding:**\n1. ❌ **Duplicates code** - Must copy all parent logic\n2. ❌ **Fragile** - If parent logic changes, must update ALL subclasses\n3. ❌ **Easy to miss steps** - Forget to call animation, scroll, etc.\n4. ❌ **Hard to maintain** - Changes require updating multiple files\n\n**Example of the problem:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Page.js (parent) - Updated\nasync show() {\n  // New: Added scroll guard\n  if (!this.smoothScroll.enabled() &amp;&amp; !this.preloader) {\n    this.smoothScroll.create();\n    this.smoothScroll.scrollTo(0, {immediate: true});\n  }\n  // New: Added analytics\n  this.trackPageView();\n  await this.animation.GSAPHideTransition(this.transitionOverlay);\n}\n\n// Home.js (subclass) - Must update manually\nasync show() {\n  // ❌ Must remember to add trackPageView() here too!",

        "contents": "└──────┬──────┘\n       │\n       │ (Component active)\n       │\n       ▼\n┌─────────────┐\n│  destroy()  │\n│             │\n│ ✅ Guard    │\n│ ✅ Flag     │\n│ ✅ Listeners│\n│ ✅ Children │\n│ ✅ Animations│\n│ ✅ DOM      │\n│ ✅ Refs     │\n│ ✅ Tracking │\n└─────────────┘\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Key Principles\n\n1. **Constructor = Pure Configuration**\n   - No DOM access\n   - No side effects\n   - Store selectors and dependencies\n\n2. **Create = Initialization**\n   - Idempotent guards\n   - DOM access allowed\n   - Set up listeners\n   - Initialize state\n\n3. **Destroy = Complete Cleanup**\n   - Remove all listeners\n   - Destroy child components\n   - Clear all references\n   - Set to null\n\n4. **Always Track Event Listeners**\n   - Store handler references\n   - Remove in destroy()\n   - Prevent memory leaks\n\n5. **Use Idempotent Guards**\n   - Prevent duplicate calls\n   - Safe to call multiple times\n   - Better error handling\n\n---\n\n## Phase 1: Constructor\n\n**Purpose**: Pure configuration, no side effects, no DOM access.\n\n### Checklist\n\n| Task | Description | Required | Example |\n|------|-------------|----------|---------|\n| **1.1** | Call &#96;super()&#96; with selectors | ✅ Yes | &#96;super({ element: \".preloader\", elements: {...} })&#96; |\n| **1.2** | Store element selectors (strings) | ✅ Yes | &#96;this.selector = \".preloader\"&#96; |\n| **1.3** | Store child element selectors | ✅ Yes | &#96;this.selectorChildren = { title: \"h1\" }&#96; |\n| **1.4** | Accept and store dependencies | ✅ If needed | &#96;this.smoothScroll = smoothScroll&#96; |\n| **1.5** | Initialize state flags | ✅ Yes | &#96;this._created = false&#96;, &#96;this._destroyed = false&#96; |\n| **1.6** | Initialize event handler tracking | ✅ If using events | &#96;this._eventHandlers = new Map()&#96; |\n| **1.7** | Initialize empty DOM references | ✅ Yes | &#96;this.element = null&#96;, &#96;this.elements = {}&#96; |\n| **1.8** | Initialize component-specific state | ✅ If needed | &#96;this.imagesLoaded = 0&#96; |\n\n### ❌ DO NOT in Constructor\n\n- ❌ Access DOM elements (&#96;document.querySelector&#96;)",

        "contents": "export default class Page {\n  constructor({ id, element, elements }) {\n    this.id = id;\n    this.selector = element;\n    this.selectorChildren = elements;\n    this._created = false;\n    this._destroyed = false;\n  }\n  \n  async create() {\n    if (this._created) return;\n    this._created = true;\n    \n    // Base initialization\n    this.element = $(this.selector);\n    this.elements = pageObject(this.selectorChildren);\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: Before components created\n    await this.onBeforeCreate?.();\n    \n    // Base component setup\n    this.smoothScroll = new SmoothScroll();\n    this.footnotes = new Footnotes({smoothScroll: this.smoothScroll});\n    this.createAnimations();\n    this.setupEventListeners();\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: After components created\n    await this.onAfterCreate?.();\n  }\n  \n  async show() {\n    if (!this.smoothScroll.enabled() &amp;&amp; !this.preloader) {\n      this.smoothScroll.create();\n      this.smoothScroll.scrollTo(0, {immediate: true});\n    }\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: Before transition\n    await this.onBeforeShow?.();\n    \n    await this.animation.GSAPHideTransition(this.transitionOverlay);\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: After transition\n    await this.onAfterShow?.();\n  }\n  \n  async hide(route) {\n    // ✅ Hook: Before transition\n    await this.onBeforeHide?.(route);\n    \n    await this.transitionManager.getTransition(route);\n    await this.animation.GSAPShowTransition(this.transitionOverlay);\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: After transition, before destroy\n    await this.onAfterHide?.(route);\n    \n    this.destroy();\n  }\n  \n  destroy() {\n    if (this._destroyed) return;\n    this._destroyed = true;\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: Before cleanup\n    this.onBeforeDestroy?.();\n    \n    this.removeEventListeners();\n    if (this.smoothScroll) {\n      this.smoothScroll.destroy();\n      this.smoothScroll = null;\n    }\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: After cleanup\n    this.onAfterDestroy?.();\n  }\n  \n  // Hook methods (optional, subclasses can override)\n  async onBeforeCreate() {} // Optional\n  async onAfterCreate() {} // Optional\n  async onBeforeShow() {} // Optional\n  async onAfterShow() {} // Optional",

        "contents": "| &#96;removeAllListeners(type)&#96; | Cleanup all handlers of a type | Removes all handlers of that type |\n| &#96;removeAllListeners()&#96; | Complete cleanup (destroy) | Removes all handlers of all types |\n\n## Example usage\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Setup\nthis.addListenerAndRegister(window, \"resize\", this.handleResize);\nthis.addListenerAndRegister(window, \"resize\", this.handleResize2);\nthis.addListenerAndRegister(window, \"scroll\", this.handleScroll);\n\n// Remove one specific handler\nthis.removeListenerAndDeregister(window, \"resize\", this.handleResize);\n// ✅ Only handleResize removed, handleResize2 and handleScroll still active\n\n// Remove all resize handlers\nthis.removeAllListeners(\"resize\");\n// ✅ Both handleResize and handleResize2 removed, handleScroll still active\n\n// Complete cleanup (in destroy())\nthis.removeAllListeners();\n// ✅ All handlers removed\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Recommendation\n\nAdd &#96;removeHandler&#96; to EventManager (Option 1) for:\n- Cleaner separation of concerns\n- Reusability\n- Better encapsulation\n\n## Summary\n\n- Don't call &#96;removeAllListeners&#96; inside &#96;removeListenerAndDeregister&#96; — it would remove all handlers.\n- Do remove the specific handler from the tracking Map.\n- Add &#96;removeHandler&#96; to EventManager, or manually remove from the Map in &#96;removeListenerAndDeregister&#96;.\n\nThis keeps the tracking Map in sync with the DOM.\n\n\n# Hooks vs Overriding: Extension Points for Subclasses\n\n## What Are Subclasses?\n\nYes! **Subclasses** are classes that inherit from a parent class using &#96;extends&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Parent class (base class)\nexport default class Page {\n  async show() { /* base implementation */ }\n}\n\n// Subclass (child class)\nexport class Home extends Page {\n  // Home \"extends\" Page - it's a subclass\n}\n\nexport class View extends Page {\n  // View \"extends\" Page - it's also a subclass\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn your codebase:\n- &#96;Home extends Page&#96; ✅\n- &#96;View extends Page&#96; ✅\n- &#96;Introduction extends Page&#96; ✅\n\nThese are all **subclasses** of &#96;Page&#96;.\n\n---\n\n## The Problem: Overriding Entire Methods\n\n### Current Situation (Good - No Overriding Yet)",

        "contents": "async show() {\n  // ❌ Must remember to add trackPageView() here too!\n  if (!this.smoothScroll.enabled() &amp;&amp; !this.preloader) {\n    this.smoothScroll.create();\n    this.smoothScroll.scrollTo(0, {immediate: true});\n  }\n  // ❌ Missing trackPageView() - bug!\n  await this.animation.GSAPHideTransition(this.transitionOverlay);\n  this.playWelcomeAnimation();\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## The Solution: Hooks (Extension Points)\n\n**Hooks** are optional methods that parent class calls at specific points, allowing subclasses to customize behavior without overriding entire methods.\n\n### How Hooks Work\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Page.js (parent) - Provides hooks\nasync show() {\n  // Base logic that ALWAYS runs\n  if (!this.smoothScroll.enabled() &amp;&amp; !this.preloader) {\n    this.smoothScroll.create();\n    this.smoothScroll.scrollTo(0, {immediate: true});\n  }\n  \n  // ✅ Hook: Call if subclass defines it\n  await this.onBeforeShow?.(); // Optional - only runs if defined\n  \n  await this.animation.GSAPHideTransition(this.transitionOverlay);\n  \n  // ✅ Hook: Call after base logic\n  await this.onAfterShow?.(); // Optional - only runs if defined\n}\n\n// Home.js (subclass) - Uses hooks\nexport class Home extends Page {\n  // ✅ Only define what you want to customize\n  async onBeforeShow() {\n    console.log('About to show home page');\n  }\n  \n  async onAfterShow() {\n    // ✅ Custom logic here\n    this.playWelcomeAnimation();\n    // Don't need to duplicate parent's show() logic!\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Benefits:**\n1. ✅ **No code duplication** - Parent logic stays in parent\n2. ✅ **Automatic updates** - Parent changes apply to all subclasses\n3. ✅ **Optional** - Only define hooks you need\n4. ✅ **Safe** - Can't break parent logic by forgetting steps\n\n---\n\n## Complete Example: Hooks vs Overriding\n\n### Scenario: Home Page Needs Custom Show Logic\n\n**With Overriding (❌ Bad):**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Page.js\nasync show() {\n  // Step 1: Initialize scroll",

        "contents": "# Component Lifecycle Management Checklist\n\nA comprehensive guide for creating, managing, and destroying components in your application.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n1. [Common Patterns](#common-patterns)\n8. [Anti-Patterns to Avoid](#anti-patterns-to-avoid)\n\n---\n\n\n## Lifecycle Phases Flow Diagram\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                    COMPONENT LIFECYCLE                       │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\n┌─────────────┐\n│ Constructor │\n│             │\n│ ✅ super()  │\n│ ✅ Selectors│\n│ ✅ Dependencies│\n│ ✅ Flags    │\n│ ✅ State    │\n└──────┬──────┘\n       │\n       ▼\n┌─────────────┐\n│   create()  │\n│             │\n│ ✅ Guard    │\n│ ✅ super.create()│\n│ ✅ Verify DOM│\n│ ✅ Process  │\n│ ✅ Listeners│\n│ ✅ Init     │\n│ ✅ Flag     │\n└──────┬──────┘\n       │\n       ▼\n┌─────────────┐      ┌─────────────┐\n│   update()  │◄─────┤  (Optional) │\n│             │      │             │\n│ ✅ Guard    │      │ ✅ Update   │\n│ ✅ Update   │      │ ✅ Re-render│\n│ ✅ Render   │      └─────────────┘\n└──────┬──────┘\n       │",

        "contents": "destroy() {\n  // ✅ Don't destroy shared services\n  // this.smoothScroll is shared, leave it alone\n  // Only destroy services owned by this component\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\n\n## Create Component Methods\n\n### 1. &#96;mount()&#96; - DOM Access &amp; Element Initialization\n\n**Purpose**: Access and initialize DOM elements (Phase 2.3-2.4 from lifecycle guide)\n\n**Responsibilities**:\n- Access DOM elements using selectors\n- Create element collections using &#96;pageObject()&#96;\n- Store references to page-specific elements (&#96;pageTransition&#96;, &#96;preloader&#96;)\n- Verify critical elements exist\n- Perform initial scroll positioning\n\n**Based on lifecycle guide**:\n- ✅ **2.3**: Verify DOM elements exist\n- ✅ **2.4**: Process/normalize element data\n\n**What it should do**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nasync mount() {\n  // Access main page element\n  this.element = $(\"main[data-template]\");\n  \n  // Verify critical element exists\n  if (!this.element) {\n    console.warn(&#96;Page ${this.id}: Main element not found&#96;);\n    return false; // Return false if critical element missing\n  }\n  \n  // Create element collections from selectors\n  this.elements = pageObject(this.selectorChildren);\n  \n  // Store references to page-specific elements\n  this.pageTransition = $(\".page-transition-overlay\");\n  this.preloader = $(\".preloader\");\n  \n  // Initial scroll position (before components initialize)\n  this.smoothScroll?.scrollTo(0, { immediate: true });\n  \n  return true; // Success\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Why separate**: DOM access is a distinct phase. Separating it makes testing easier and clarifies dependencies.\n\n---\n\n### 2. &#96;initComponents()&#96; - Initialize Child Components\n\n**Purpose**: Initialize child components and services (Phase 2.5 from lifecycle guide)\n\n**Responsibilities**:\n- Initialize child components that depend on DOM elements\n- Set up component-specific configurations\n- Call component setup methods\n\n**Based on lifecycle guide**:\n- ✅ **2.5**: Initialize child components\n\n**What it should do**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nasync initComponents() {\n  // Initialize footnotes component (depends on DOM being mounted)",

        "contents": "async show() {\n  // Step 1: Initialize scroll\n  if (!this.smoothScroll.enabled() &amp;&amp; !this.preloader) {\n    this.smoothScroll.create();\n    this.smoothScroll.scrollTo(0, {immediate: true});\n  }\n  \n  // Step 2: Track analytics\n  this.trackPageView();\n  \n  // Step 3: Hide transition\n  await this.animation.GSAPHideTransition(this.transitionOverlay);\n  \n  // Step 4: Focus management\n  this.focusMainContent();\n}\n\n// Home.js - Must override entire method\nasync show() {\n  // ❌ Must duplicate all 4 steps\n  if (!this.smoothScroll.enabled() &amp;&amp; !this.preloader) {\n    this.smoothScroll.create();\n    this.smoothScroll.scrollTo(0, {immediate: true});\n  }\n  this.trackPageView(); // ❌ Copy-paste\n  await this.animation.GSAPHideTransition(this.transitionOverlay); // ❌ Copy-paste\n  this.focusMainContent(); // ❌ Copy-paste\n  \n  // ✅ Only this is new\n  this.playWelcomeAnimation();\n}\n\n// Problem: If Page.show() changes, must update Home.show() too!\n// Problem: 10 lines of duplication\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**With Hooks (✅ Good):**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Page.js - Provides hooks\nasync show() {\n  // Step 1: Initialize scroll\n  if (!this.smoothScroll.enabled() &amp;&amp; !this.preloader) {\n    this.smoothScroll.create();\n    this.smoothScroll.scrollTo(0, {immediate: true});\n  }\n  \n  // Step 2: Track analytics\n  this.trackPageView();\n  \n  // ✅ Hook: Before transition\n  await this.onBeforeShow?.();\n  \n  // Step 3: Hide transition\n  await this.animation.GSAPHideTransition(this.transitionOverlay);\n  \n  // Step 4: Focus management\n  this.focusMainContent();\n  \n  // ✅ Hook: After everything\n  await this.onAfterShow?.();\n}\n\n// Home.js - Only defines what's needed\nexport class Home extends Page {\n  // ✅ Only 1 line - just the custom logic\n  async onAfterShow() {\n    this.playWelcomeAnimation();\n  }\n}\n\n// ✅ No duplication\n// ✅ Automatic updates\n// ✅ Clean and simple\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Pros and Cons: Overriding vs Hooks\n\n### Overriding (Current Pattern - If You Used It)\n\n**Pros:**\n- ✅ Full control - can change any part\n- ✅ Simple concept - just override method",

        "contents": "5. Override points: Subclasses can override specific phases\n6. Aligns with lifecycle guide: Follows the documented patterns\n\n---\n\n## Additional Considerations\n\n### Error Handling\nEach function can return a boolean or throw, allowing &#96;create()&#96; to handle failures:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nasync create() {\n  if (this._created) return;\n  \n  try {\n    await this.beforeCreate?.();\n    \n    if (!(await this.mount())) {\n      throw new Error(&#96;Page ${this.id}: Mount failed&#96;);\n    }\n    \n    await this.initComponents();\n    this.initAnimations();\n    await this.ready();\n    \n    this._created = true;\n    await this.afterCreate?.();\n  } catch (error) {\n    console.error(&#96;Page ${this.id}: Creation failed:&#96;, error);\n    // Cleanup partial creation if needed\n    throw error; // Let parent handle\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\n# Separating Configuration from Initialization in App.js\n\n## Current Problem\n\nYour constructor is doing too much:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nconstructor() {\n  setupHelpers();              // Side effect (modifies prototype)\n  this.createServices();        // Creates state\n  this.pageConfig = setupPageConfig(); // Configuration (okay)\n  this.setupPages();           // DOM access, async operations\n  this.setupApp();             // Event listeners\n  this.setupEventListeners();  // Event listeners\n  this.createPreloader();      // Creates components\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Issues:**\n1. ❌ Mixing configuration and initialization\n2. ❌ Side effects in constructor\n3. ❌ Async operations (&#96;setupPages()&#96; is async but not awaited)\n4. ❌ Hard to test\n5. ❌ Can't create instance without initializing\n\n---\n\n## Solution: Two-Phase Initialization\n\n### Pattern: Constructor (Config) + init() (Initialization)\n\n**Phase 1: Constructor - Configuration Only**\n- Store configuration\n- Accept dependencies\n- No side effects\n- No DOM access\n- No async operations\n\n**Phase 2: init() - Initialization**\n- All side effects\n- DOM access\n- Async operations\n- Creates components\n\n---\n\n## Recommended Approach\n\n### Option 1: init() Method (Recommended)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js",

        "contents": "&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nconstructor({ id, element, elements }) {\n  this.id = id;\n  this.selector = element;\n  this.selectorChildren = elements;\n  \n  // ✅ Initialize lifecycle flags\n  this._created = false;\n  this._destroyed = false;\n  this._listenersSetup = false;\n}\n\nasync create() {\n  // ✅ Guard: Check if already created\n  if (this._created) {\n    console.warn(&#96;Page ${this.id}.create() called multiple times&#96;);\n    return; // Early return - do nothing\n  }\n  \n  // ✅ Guard against recreating destroyed page\n  if (this._destroyed) {\n    throw new Error(&#96;Cannot create destroyed page: ${this.id}. Create new instance.&#96;);\n  }\n  \n  // ✅ Set flag BEFORE doing work\n  this._created = true;\n  \n  // Now safe to do initialization\n  this.element = $(this.selector);\n  this.elements = pageObject(this.selectorChildren);\n  this.transitionOverlay = document.querySelector(\".page-transition-overlay\");\n  \n  // ✅ Check before creating instances (or inject dependencies)\n  if (!this.transitionManager) {\n    this.transitionManager = new TransitionManager();\n  }\n  this.transitionManager.setupTransitionTemplates();\n  \n  if (!this.smoothScroll) {\n    this.smoothScroll = new SmoothScroll();\n  }\n  \n  this.footnotes = new Footnotes({smoothScroll: this.smoothScroll});\n  this.createAnimations();\n  this.setupEventListeners();\n  this.preloader = document.querySelector(\".preloader\");\n  this.smoothScroll.scrollTo(0, {immediate: true});\n}\n\ndestroy() {\n  // ✅ Guard: Check if already destroyed",

        "contents": "**Based on lifecycle guide**:\n- ✅ **2.6**: Set up event listeners\n- ✅ **2.8**: Start async operations (if any final async tasks needed)\n\n**What it should do**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nasync ready() {\n  // Set up event listeners (idempotent guard already in setupEventListeners)\n  this.setupEventListeners();\n  \n  // Future: Any final async operations\n  // await this.preloadCriticalAssets();\n  \n  // Future: Emit ready event if needed\n  // this.emit('page-ready', { pageId: this.id });\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Why separate**: Final setup tasks should run after everything else is initialized. This is the last step before the component is fully ready.\n\n---\n\n## Refactored &#96;create()&#96; Method\n\nHere's how the refactored &#96;create()&#96; would orchestrate these functions:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n/**\n * Create a page object of elements\n * Initialize any other components for the page\n * Orchestrates: mount → initComponents → initAnimations → ready\n */\nasync create() {\n  // ✅ 2.1: Idempotent guard (from lifecycle guide)\n  if (this._created) {\n    console.warn(&#96;Page ${this.id}.create() called multiple times&#96;);\n    return;\n  }\n\n  // Lifecycle hook: before creation starts\n  await this.beforeCreate?.();\n\n  // Phase 1: Mount DOM elements\n  const mounted = await this.mount();\n  if (!mounted) {\n    console.error(&#96;Page ${this.id}: Failed to mount, aborting creation&#96;);\n    return;\n  }\n\n  // Phase 2: Initialize child components\n  await this.initComponents();\n\n  // Phase 3: Initialize animations\n  this.initAnimations();\n\n  // Phase 4: Final setup (event listeners, etc.)\n  await this.ready();\n\n  // ✅ 2.9: Mark as created (from lifecycle guide)\n  this._created = true;\n\n  // Lifecycle hook: after creation completes\n  await this.afterCreate?.();\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Benefits of This Approach\n\n1. Single responsibility: Each function has one clear purpose\n2. Testability: Each phase can be tested independently\n3. Extensibility: Easy to add new initialization steps\n4. Debugging: Easier to identify which phase failed\n5. Override points: Subclasses can override specific phases\n6. Aligns with lifecycle guide: Follows the documented patterns\n\n---",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./documentation/guides/COMPONENT_GUIDE.md",

          "endPosition": {
            "line": 2804
          }
        },
        "contents": "Currently, tracking is only in &#96;on()&#96; and &#96;once()&#96;, so DOM listeners (e.g., &#96;window.addEventListener&#96;, &#96;element.addEventListener&#96;) aren't tracked. Generalizing the API so components can track any listener registration.\n\nHere's a generalized event lifecycle API:\n\n## Generalized Event Lifecycle API\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript:app/components/Component.js\nexport default class Component extends EventTarget {\n  constructor({ element, elements }) {\n    super();\n    this.selector = element;\n    this.selectorChildren = { ...elements };\n    this.eventTarget = new EventTarget();\n    this.eventHandlers = new Map(); // Track ALL handlers (Component + DOM)\n    this.element = null;\n    this.elements = {};\n  }\n\n  // ... existing create() and emit() ...\n\n  /**\n   * Add an event listener for the given event type (Component events)\n   */\n  on(type, callback) {\n    const handler = (event) =&gt; callback(event.detail);\n    this.eventTarget.addEventListener(type, handler);\n    \n    // ✅ Use generalized tracking method\n    this.addHandler(type, handler, this.eventTarget);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Add an event listener that will be removed after the first event\n   */\n  once(type, callback) {\n    const handler = (event) =&gt; {\n      callback(event.detail);\n      this.eventTarget.removeEventListener(type, handler);\n      this.removeHandler(type, handler, this.eventTarget);\n    };\n    this.eventTarget.addEventListener(type, handler);\n    \n    // ✅ Use generalized tracking method\n    this.addHandler(type, handler, this.eventTarget);\n  }\n\n  // ============================================\n  // GENERALIZED EVENT LIFECYCLE METHODS\n  // ============================================\n\n  /**\n   * Add a handler to tracking (for any event target)\n   * @param {string} type - Event type\n   * @param {Function} handler - Handler function\n   * @param {EventTarget} target - Event target (default: this.eventTarget)\n   */\n  addHandler(type, handler, target = this.eventTarget) {\n    const key = this._getHandlerKey(type, target);\n    ",

        },
        "contents": "  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Example: Lazy Loading Content\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nexport class MyPage extends Page {\n  async afterCreate() {\n    // Load additional content after page is created\n    const response = await fetch('/api/additional-content');\n    const data = await response.json();\n    this.renderAdditionalContent(data);\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Creating Custom Components\n\n### Step 1: Extend Component Base Class\n\nCreate &#96;app/components/MyComponent.js&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nimport Component from \"./Component.js\";\nimport { SELECTORS, EVENTS } from \"../utilities/Constants.js\";\n\nexport class MyComponent extends Component {\n  constructor(options = {}) {\n    super({\n      element: SELECTORS.MY_COMPONENT,\n      elements: {\n        button: \".my-component__button\",\n        content: \".my-component__content\",\n      },\n    });\n  }\n\n  create() {\n    super.create(); // Sets up this.element and this.elements\n    \n    // Component-specific initialization\n    this.setupEventListeners();\n  }\n  \n  setupEventListeners() {\n    if (this.elements.button) {\n      this.addListenerAndRegister(\n        this.elements.button,\n        EVENTS.CLICK,\n        this.handleButtonClick.bind(this)\n      );\n    }\n  }\n  \n  handleButtonClick(event) {\n    // Handle click\n    this.emit('button-clicked', { component: this });\n  }\n  \n  destroy() {\n    // Clean up event listeners\n    this.removeAllListeners();\n    \n    // Clear references\n    this.element = null;\n    this.elements = null;\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 2: Use Component in Page",

        "contents": "- Current page template\n\n**Usage:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Register a page class\nregistryService.setPage('home', Home);\n\n// Get a page class\nconst HomeClass = registryService.getPage('home');\n\n// Track current page\nregistryService.setCurrentPage(pageInstance);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3. Manager Pattern\nMultiple managers coordinate specific domains:\n\n- **RouterPageManager** (&#96;app/router/RouterPageManager.js&#96;): Manages page content updates, DOM manipulation, and page metadata\n- **AnimationsService** (&#96;app/services/AnimationsService.js&#96;): Manages page animations lifecycle, IntersectionObserver setup, and animation cleanup\n- **TransitionsService** (&#96;app/services/TransitionsService.js&#96;): Manages page transition overlays, image preloading, and transition templates\n\n### 4. Component Base Class Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/components/Component.js&#96;\n\nAll components inherit from a base &#96;Component&#96; class that provides:\n- Event management (via EventManager)\n- Element selection and caching\n- Lifecycle hooks (create, destroy)\n- Event emission/listening\n\n**Example:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nclass Preloader extends Component {\n  constructor() {\n    super({\n      element: SELECTORS.PRELOADER,\n      elements: { /* child selectors */ }\n    });\n  }\n  \n  create() {\n    super.create(); // Sets up this.element and this.elements\n    // Component-specific initialization\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 5. Lifecycle Hooks Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/pages/Page.js&#96;\n\nPages implement a clear lifecycle with optional hooks:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nclass Page {\n  async create() {\n    await this.beforeCreate?.()  // Optional hook\n    await this.createElements();\n    await this.createComponents();\n    this.createPageAnimations();\n    this.createPage();\n    await this.afterCreate?.()   // Optional hook\n  }\n  \n  async show() {\n    await this.beforeShow?.()\n    // Show logic\n    await this.afterShow?.()\n  }\n  \n  async hide(route) {\n    await this.beforeHide?.()\n    // Hide logic\n    await this.afterHide?.()\n  }\n  \n  async destroy() {\n    await this.beforeDestroy?.()\n    // Cleanup logic\n    await this.afterDestroy?.()\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 6. Orchestrator Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/services/Router.js&#96;\n\nThe &#96;Router&#96; orchestrates the page navigation lifecycle:\n\n1. **beforePageUpdate**: Validates route\n2. **startPageUpdate**: Hides current page, updates DOM, loads new page\n3. **afterPageUpdate**: Creates and shows new page\n\nThis pattern ensures a consistent, testable navigation flow.",

        "contents": "export class EventManager {\n\n\n  /**\n   * Add a DOM event listener and automatically register it for cleanup\n   * Use this instead of addEventListener + registerEvent\n   * @param {EventTarget} target - The event target (element, window, document, etc.)\n   * @param {string} type - The event type\n   * @param {Function} handler - The event handler function\n   * @param {Object} options - Optional addEventListener options\n   */\n  addListenerAndRegister(target, type, handler, options) {\n    // Support both native addEventListener and element prototype .on()\n    if (typeof target.addEventListener === \"function\") {\n      target.addEventListener(type, handler, options);\n    } else if (typeof target.on === \"function\") {\n      target.on(type, handler, options);\n    } else {\n      throw createError(ERROR_CODES.VALIDATION_ERROR, { message: 'Target must support addEventListener or .on()' });\n    }\n\n    // Automatically register for cleanup\n    this.registerEvent(type, handler, target);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Remove a specific DOM event listener\n   * @param {EventTarget} target - The event target\n   * @param {string} type - The event type\n   * @param {Function} handler - The event handler function\n   */\n}",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./documentation/guides/COMPONENT_GUIDE.md",
        "range": {

          "endPosition": {

        },
        "contents": "| &#96;removeAllListeners(type)&#96; | Cleanup all handlers of a type | Removes all handlers of that type |\n| &#96;removeAllListeners()&#96; | Complete cleanup (destroy) | Removes all handlers of all types |\n\n## Example usage\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Setup\nthis.addListenerAndRegister(window, \"resize\", this.handleResize);\nthis.addListenerAndRegister(window, \"resize\", this.handleResize2);\nthis.addListenerAndRegister(window, \"scroll\", this.handleScroll);\n\n// Remove one specific handler\nthis.removeListenerAndDeregister(window, \"resize\", this.handleResize);\n// ✅ Only handleResize removed, handleResize2 and handleScroll still active\n\n// Remove all resize handlers\nthis.removeAllListeners(\"resize\");\n// ✅ Both handleResize and handleResize2 removed, handleScroll still active\n\n// Complete cleanup (in destroy())\nthis.removeAllListeners();\n// ✅ All handlers removed\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Recommendation\n\nAdd &#96;removeHandler&#96; to EventManager (Option 1) for:\n- Cleaner separation of concerns\n- Reusability\n- Better encapsulation\n\n## Summary\n\n- Don't call &#96;removeAllListeners&#96; inside &#96;removeListenerAndDeregister&#96; — it would remove all handlers.\n- Do remove the specific handler from the tracking Map.\n- Add &#96;removeHandler&#96; to EventManager, or manually remove from the Map in &#96;removeListenerAndDeregister&#96;.\n\nThis keeps the tracking Map in sync with the DOM.\n\n\n# Hooks vs Overriding: Extension Points for Subclasses\n\n## What Are Subclasses?\n\nYes! **Subclasses** are classes that inherit from a parent class using &#96;extends&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Parent class (base class)\nexport default class Page {\n  async show() { /* base implementation */ }\n}\n\n// Subclass (child class)\nexport class Home extends Page {\n  // Home \"extends\" Page - it's a subclass\n}\n\nexport class View extends Page {\n  // View \"extends\" Page - it's also a subclass\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn your codebase:\n- &#96;Home extends Page&#96; ✅\n- &#96;View extends Page&#96; ✅\n- &#96;Introduction extends Page&#96; ✅\n\nThese are all **subclasses** of &#96;Page&#96;.\n\n---\n\n## The Problem: Overriding Entire Methods\n\n### Current Situation (Good - No Overriding Yet)",

        "contents": "- &#96;DefaultHideStrategy&#96; - handles standard hide behavior\n- Subclasses can inject custom strategies\n\n**Use Case**: When different page types need different show/hide behaviors without overriding entire methods.\n\n### Option 3: Command Pattern for Lifecycle Operations\n\nEncapsulate lifecycle operations as commands:\n\n- &#96;CreatePageCommand&#96;, &#96;DestroyPageCommand&#96;, &#96;ShowPageCommand&#96;, &#96;HidePageCommand&#96;\n- Commands can be queued, logged, or undone\n\n**Use Case**: If you need lifecycle operation history, undo/redo, or async operation queuing.\n\n### Option 4: Observer Pattern for Lifecycle Events\n\nReplace optional hook methods (&#96;beforeCreate?()&#96;, &#96;afterShow?()&#96;) with an event emitter:\n\n- Page emits lifecycle events: &#96;create:before&#96;, &#96;create:after&#96;, &#96;show:before&#96;, etc.\n- Subclasses or external services subscribe to events\n- More flexible than method overrides\n\n**Use Case**: When multiple systems need to react to page lifecycle events.\n\n## Recommended Implementation: Hybrid Approach\n\nCombine **Option 1 (Composition)** with **Option 2 (Strategy)** for maximum flexibility:\n\n### Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nPage (Facade)\n├── PageElementManager (handles DOM)\n├── PageComponentManager (handles components)  \n├── PageLifecycleManager (orchestrates lifecycle)\n├── PageStateManager (tracks state)\n└── ShowStrategy / HideStrategy (pluggable behaviors)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Benefits\n\n- **Single Responsibility**: Each manager has one clear purpose\n- **Testability**: Managers can be tested independently\n- **Maintainability**: Changes to one concern don't affect others\n- **Flexibility**: Strategies allow behavior customization\n- **Reusability**: Managers can be reused in other contexts\n\n### Migration Path\n\n1. **Phase 1**: Extract managers without changing Page API (internal refactor)\n2. **Phase 2**: Update Page to use managers via composition\n3. **Phase 3**: (Optional) Add Strategy pattern for show/hide if needed\n4. **Phase 4**: (Optional) Replace hooks with Observer pattern if multiple subscribers needed\n\n## Code Size Reduction Estimate\n\n- Current: ~226 lines",

        "contents": "export class EventManager {\n\n\n  /**\n   * Remove a specific event handler from tracking\n   * @param {string} type - The event type\n   * @param {Function} handler - The specific handler to remove\n   * @param {EventTarget} target - The event target\n   */\n  removeHandler(type, handler, target) {\n    const handlers = this.eventHandlers.get(type) || [];\n    const index = handlers.findIndex(\n      (h) =&gt; h.handler === handler &amp;&amp; h.target === target\n    );\n\n    if (index &gt; -1) {\n      handlers.splice(index, 1);\n      if (handlers.length === 0) {\n        this.eventHandlers.delete(type);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}",

**RouterResolver**: Validates routes\n- **RouterHistory**: Manages browser history\n\n### Recommended Improvements\n\n#### 1. **Observer Pattern for Page Lifecycle Events**\n\nInstead of direct method calls, use events for lifecycle hooks:\nript\nclass PageLifecycleManager {\n  constructor(eventBus) {\n    this.eventBus = eventBus;\n  }\n  \n  async transitionPage(fromPage, toPage, route) {\n    this.eventBus.emit('page:before-hide', { page: fromPage, route });\n    await fromPage.hide(route);\n    this.eventBus.emit('page:after-hide', { page: fromPage });\n    \n    this.eventBus.emit('page:before-show', { page: toPage });\n    await toPage.show();\n    this.eventBus.emit('page:after-show', { page: toPage });\n  }\n}**Benefits:**\n- Decouples components\n- Easy to add logging, analytics, error tracking\n- Allows plugins/extensions\n- Better testability\n\n#### 2. **Pipeline Pattern for Navigation Flow**\n\nBreak navigation into a pipeline of steps:\nascript\nclass NavigationPipeline {\n  constructor() {\n    this.steps = [];\n  }\n  \n  addStep(step) {\n    this.steps.push(step);\n    return this;\n  }\n  \n  async execute(context) {\n    for (const step of this.steps) {\n      context = await step.execute(context);\n      if (context.shouldAbort) break;\n    }\n    return context;\n  }\n}\n\n// Usage:\nconst pipeline = new NavigationPipeline()\n  .addStep(new ValidateRouteStep())\n  .addStep(new HideCurrentPageStep())\n  .addStep(new UpdateDOMStep())\n  .addStep(new LoadPageClassStep())\n  .addStep(new ShowNewPageStep());\n\nawait pipeline.execute({ href, router: this });**Benefits:**\n- Easy to add/remove steps\n- Clear flow visualization\n- Can add middleware (logging, error handling)\n- Testable individual steps\n\n#### 3. **Repository Pattern for Page Storage**\n\nMake PageRegistry a true repository:\n\nclass PageRepository {\n  constructor() {\n    this.pageClasses = new Map(); // Page         "contents": "export class EventManager {\n\n\n  /**\n   * Remove event listeners\n   * @param {string} [type] - Optional event type.         "contents": "The NodeList cleanup you mentioned is the **most important** part!\n\n\n\n\n\n# Event Listener Patterns\n\nLet’s break down the **Event Listener Lifecycle Management pattern** (a.k.a. **Handler Registry** or **Listener Tracking**) step-by-step 👇\n\n---\n\n## 🔹 1. The Core Idea\n\nEvent listeners (like &#96;element.addEventListener&#96;) need to be:\n\n* **Registered** when a component or feature is initialized.\n* **Removed** (via &#96;removeEventListener&#96;) when that component or feature is destroyed, unmounted, or replaced.\n\nIf you **don’t remove** them, they can:\n\n* Cause **memory leaks** (holding onto DOM nodes or closures).\n* Cause **duplicate handlers** when re-initializing UI.\n* Trigger **logic bugs** because old listeners remain active.\n\nSo — the **Event Listener Lifecycle Management pattern** formalizes **tracking, cleaning up, and re-binding** listeners as a consistent part of your component or app lifecycle.\n\n---\n\n## 🔹 2. What It Looks Like Conceptually\n\nInstead of sprinkling event listeners everywhere like:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nwindow.addEventListener('resize', handleResize);\nbutton.addEventListener('click', handleClick);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n…you maintain a **registry** of listeners and their teardown logic:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nconst listenerRegistry = [];\n\nfunction addListener(target, event, handler, options) {\n  target.addEventListener(event, handler, options);\n  listenerRegistry.push(() =&gt; target.removeEventListener(event, handler, options));\n}\n\nfunction removeAllListeners() {\n  listenerRegistry.forEach(off =&gt; off());\n  listenerRegistry.length = 0; // clear registry\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNow your lifecycle logic is explicit:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nfunction initUI() {\n  addListener(window, 'resize', handleResize);\n  addListener(button, 'click', handleClick);\n}\n\nfunction destroyUI() {\n  removeAllListeners(); // safely clean up\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## 🔹 3. Why This Pattern Exists\n\n### 🧠 Problem it Solves\n\n* Avoids **leaking listeners** when elements are removed from the DOM.\n* Avoids **duplicate event triggers** after re-initialization.\n* Keeps teardown logic **automatic** and consistent.\n\n### ✅ Benefits",

        },
        "contents": "export class EventManager {\n\n\n  /**\n   * Remove a specific DOM event listener\n   * @param {EventTarget} target - The event target\n   * @param {string} type - The event type\n   * @param {Function} handler - The event handler function\n   */\n  removeListenerAndDeregister(target, type, handler) {\n    // Remove from DOM\n    if (typeof target.removeEventListener === \"function\") {\n      target.removeEventListener(type, handler);\n    } else if (typeof target.off === \"function\") {\n      target.off(type, handler);\n    }\n\n    // ✅ Remove from tracking (specific handler only)\n    this.removeHandler(type, handler, target);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Remove a specific event handler from tracking\n   * @param {string} type - The event type\n   * @param {Function} handler - The specific handler to remove\n   * @param {EventTarget} target - The event target\n   */\n}",

If provided, removes only that type. If omitted, removes all listeners.\n   * Call this in destroy() to prevent memory leaks\n   */\n}",

      "codeBlock": {
