        "contents": "3. For DOM event listeners (window, document, elements)\n   - Continue manual tracking as needed\n   - These are simpler cases\n\n### Why this works\n- Components get the pattern automatically\n- Non-Component classes can opt in when needed\n- Avoids mixin complexity\n- Keeps the codebase simple\n\n### When to extract to a mixin\nExtract only if:\n- Multiple non-Component classes need event lifecycle\n- You want to test event lifecycle in isolation\n- You need to share event lifecycle across unrelated classes\n\nRight now, SmoothScroll is the only non-Component class with listeners, and it's a simple case (one window resize listener). Manual tracking is fine there.\n\nRecommendation: Keep it in Component.js for now. It's simpler, all components benefit, and the few edge cases can be handled manually.\n\n\n\n## The Data Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Map structure:\n_eventHandlers = Map {\n  \"preloader-complete\" =&gt; [handler1, handler2, handler3],\n  \"navigation-changed\" =&gt; [handler1],\n  \"footnote-click\"     =&gt; [handler1, handler2]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Why an Array?\n\nEach event type can have multiple listeners. The array stores all handlers for that type so you can:\n1. Remove all handlers for a specific event type\n2. Remove all handlers when the component is destroyed\n3. Support multiple listeners on the same event\n\n## Example: Multiple Listeners\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Component can have multiple listeners for same event\npreloader.on(\"preloader-complete\", handler1);\npreloader.on(\"preloader-complete\", handler2);\npreloader.on(\"preloader-complete\", handler3);\n\n// Map structure:\n// \"preloader-complete\" =&gt; [handler1, handler2, handler3]\n\n// When cleaning up:\npreloader.removeAllListeners(\"preloader-complete\");\n// Removes all 3 handlers in one call\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis pattern supports multiple listeners per event type and enables bulk cleanup.\n\n\n\n# Component Versus Global Window DOM Event Tracking\n\nCurrently, tracking is only in &#96;on()&#96; and &#96;once()&#96;, so DOM listeners (e.g., &#96;window.addEventListener&#96;, &#96;element.addEventListener&#96;) aren't tracked. Generalizing the API so components can track any listener registration.\n\nHere's a generalized event lifecycle API:\n\n## Generalized Event Lifecycle API",

        "contents": "- Current page template\n\n**Usage:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Register a page class\nregistryService.setPage('home', Home);\n\n// Get a page class\nconst HomeClass = registryService.getPage('home');\n\n// Track current page\nregistryService.setCurrentPage(pageInstance);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3. Manager Pattern\nMultiple managers coordinate specific domains:\n\n- **RouterPageManager** (&#96;app/router/RouterPageManager.js&#96;): Manages page content updates, DOM manipulation, and page metadata\n- **AnimationsService** (&#96;app/services/AnimationsService.js&#96;): Manages page animations lifecycle, IntersectionObserver setup, and animation cleanup\n- **TransitionsService** (&#96;app/services/TransitionsService.js&#96;): Manages page transition overlays, image preloading, and transition templates\n\n### 4. Component Base Class Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/components/Component.js&#96;\n\nAll components inherit from a base &#96;Component&#96; class that provides:\n- Event management (via EventManager)\n- Element selection and caching\n- Lifecycle hooks (create, destroy)\n- Event emission/listening\n\n**Example:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nclass Preloader extends Component {\n  constructor() {\n    super({\n      element: SELECTORS.PRELOADER,\n      elements: { /* child selectors */ }\n    });\n  }\n  \n  create() {\n    super.create(); // Sets up this.element and this.elements\n    // Component-specific initialization\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 5. Lifecycle Hooks Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/pages/Page.js&#96;\n\nPages implement a clear lifecycle with optional hooks:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nclass Page {\n  async create() {\n    await this.beforeCreate?.()  // Optional hook\n    await this.createElements();\n    await this.createComponents();\n    this.createPageAnimations();\n    this.createPage();\n    await this.afterCreate?.()   // Optional hook\n  }\n  \n  async show() {\n    await this.beforeShow?.()\n    // Show logic\n    await this.afterShow?.()\n  }\n  \n  async hide(route) {\n    await this.beforeHide?.()\n    // Hide logic\n    await this.afterHide?.()\n  }\n  \n  async destroy() {\n    await this.beforeDestroy?.()\n    // Cleanup logic\n    await this.afterDestroy?.()\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 6. Orchestrator Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/services/Router.js&#96;\n\nThe &#96;Router&#96; orchestrates the page navigation lifecycle:\n\n1. **beforePageUpdate**: Validates route\n2. **startPageUpdate**: Hides current page, updates DOM, loads new page\n3. **afterPageUpdate**: Creates and shows new page\n\nThis pattern ensures a consistent, testable navigation flow.",

        "contents": "If you only need to track Component events and don't need to track DOM events separately:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript:app/components/Component.js\n/**\n * Simplified generalized API - just for Component events\n */\nexport default class Component extends EventTarget {\n  constructor({ element, elements }) {\n    super();\n    this.selector = element;\n    this.selectorChildren = { ...elements };\n    this.eventTarget = new EventTarget();\n    this.eventHandlers = new Map();\n    this.element = null;\n    this.elements = {};\n  }\n\n  // ... existing create() and emit() ...\n\n  on(type, callback) {\n    const handler = (event) =&gt; callback(event.detail);\n    this.eventTarget.addEventListener(type, handler);\n    this.addHandler(type, handler);\n  }\n\n  once(type, callback) {\n    const handler = (event) =&gt; {\n      callback(event.detail);\n      this.eventTarget.removeEventListener(type, handler);\n      this.removeHandler(type, handler);\n    };\n    this.eventTarget.addEventListener(type, handler);\n    this.addHandler(type, handler);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Add a handler to tracking\n   */\n  addHandler(type, handler) {\n    if (!this.eventHandlers.has(type)) {\n      this.eventHandlers.set(type, []);\n    }\n    this.eventHandlers.get(type).push(handler);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Check if handlers exist for event type\n   */\n  hasHandler(type) {\n    return this.eventHandlers.has(type) &amp;&amp; this.eventHandlers.get(type).length &gt; 0;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Remove a specific handler\n   */\n  removeHandler(type, handler) {\n    const handlers = this.eventHandlers.get(type) || [];\n    const index = handlers.indexOf(handler);\n    if (index &gt; -1) {\n      this.eventTarget.removeEventListener(type, handler);\n      handlers.splice(index, 1);\n      if (handlers.length === 0) {\n        this.eventHandlers.delete(type);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Remove all handlers for a specific event type\n   */\n  removeAllHandlers(type) {\n    const handlers = this.eventHandlers.get(type) || [];",

        "contents": "#### 20. Implement Command Pattern for Navigation Actions\n**Issue:** Navigation flow is hard to test and undo\n**Solution:** Use Command pattern:avascript\nclass NavigationCommand {\n  constructor(router, href) {\n    this.router = router;\n    this.href = href;\n    this.previousState = null;\n  }\n  \n  async execute() {\n    this.previousState = this.router.saveState();\n    await this.router.performNavigation(this.href);\n  }\n  \n  async undo() {\n    if (this.previousState) {\n      await this.router.restoreState(this.previousState);\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n#### 21. Extract Page Factory Pattern\n**Issue:** Page creation logic is scattered across PageLoader\n**Solution:** Create PageFactory:pt\nclass PageFactory {\n  constructor(dependencies) {\n    this.dependencies = dependencies;\n  }\n  \n  async createPage(template, options = {}) {\n    const PageClass = await this.loadPageClass(template);\n    const page = new PageClass({\n      element: options.element || &#96;main[data-template=\"${template}\"]&#96;,\n      ...this.dependencies,\n      ...options\n    });\n    \n    if (options.autoCreate) {\n      await page.create();\n    }\n    \n    return page;\n  }\n}\n\n#### 22. Implement Event-Driven Architecture\n**Issue:** Components are tightly coupled\n**Solution:** Use event bus for communication:pt\nclass EventBus {\n  constructor() {\n    this.listeners = new Map();\n  }\n  \n  on(event, handler) {\n    if (!this.listeners.has(event)) {\n      this.listeners.set(event, []);\n    }\n    this.listeners.get(event).push(handler);\n  }\n  \n  emit(event, data) {\n    const handlers = this.listeners.get(event) || [];\n    handlers.forEach(handler =&gt; handler(data));\n  }\n}\n\n// Usage:\neventBus.emit('page:before-hide', { page, route });\neventBus.emit('page:after-show', { page });---\n\n## Design Pattern &amp; Architecture Suggestions\n\n### Current Architecture Analysis\n\nThe current architecture follows a **Service Layer Pattern** with clear separation of concerns:\n- **RouterRefactor**: Orchestrates navigation flow\n- **PageLoader**: Handles page class loading and instantiation\n- **PageRegistry**: Manages page instances and classes",

        "contents": "### Debugging Tips\n\n1. **Add logging to track handler execution order:**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n   console.log('Handler fired:', handlerName, 'Phase:', event.eventPhase);\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. **Check &#96;event.defaultPrevented&#96;:**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n   console.log('Default prevented?', event.defaultPrevented);\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. **Monitor event propagation:**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n   console.log('Event phase:', event.eventPhase); // 1=capture, 2=target, 3=bubbling\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## 7. Summary\n\nThe core issue was **conflicting event handlers** where:\n- Navigation's direct handlers executed before Router's delegation handler\n- Missing or delayed &#96;preventDefault()&#96; calls allowed browser navigation\n- Async operations created timing windows for default behavior\n\nThe fix required:\n- Using **capture phase** to ensure Router's handler runs first\n- Using **&#96;stopImmediatePropagation()&#96;** to prevent Navigation's handler from running\n- Moving menu-closing logic to Router to centralize navigation handling\n- Adding a **navigation guard** to prevent concurrent navigations\n\n**Key Takeaway:** When implementing event delegation in SPAs, ensure critical handlers run first (capture phase), prevent default immediately, and coordinate multiple handlers to avoid conflicts.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Deep Dive: Event Phases, Capture, and Propagation Control\n\n### Understanding the Event Propagation Lifecycle\n\nWhen a user interacts with a DOM element (e.g., clicks a link), the browser fires an event that travels through the DOM in a specific order. Understanding this lifecycle is crucial for implementing robust event handling.\n\n### The Three Phases of Event Propagation\n\nEvery DOM event goes through three distinct phases:\n\n#### Phase 1: CAPTURE Phase (Top → Target)\n\n**Direction:** &#96;document&#96; → &#96;html&#96; → &#96;body&#96; → ... → target element  \n**Purpose:** Allows parent elements to intercept events **before** they reach the target  \n**When it runs:** First, immediately after the event is dispatched  \n**Event Phase Value:** &#96;Event.CAPTURING_PHASE&#96; (1)\n\nDuring capture, the event travels **down** the DOM tree from the root (&#96;document&#96;) toward the target element. Handlers registered with &#96;{ capture: true }&#96; execute in this phase.\n\n**Visual Flow:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nUser clicks &lt;a&gt; inside &lt;nav&gt; inside &lt;body&gt;\n    ↓",

        "contents": "export class EventLifecycle {\n  constructor() {\n    this.eventTarget = new EventTarget();\n    this._eventHandlers = new Map();\n  }\n\n  on(type, callback) {\n    const handler = (event) =&gt; callback(event.detail);\n    this.eventTarget.addEventListener(type, handler);\n    \n    if (!this._eventHandlers.has(type)) {\n      this._eventHandlers.set(type, []);\n    }\n    this._eventHandlers.get(type).push(handler);\n  }\n\n  once(type, callback) {\n    const handler = (event) =&gt; {\n      callback(event.detail);\n      this.eventTarget.removeEventListener(type, handler);\n      \n      const handlers = this._eventHandlers.get(type);\n      if (handlers) {\n        const index = handlers.indexOf(handler);\n        if (index &gt; -1) handlers.splice(index, 1);\n      }\n    };\n    this.eventTarget.addEventListener(type, handler);\n    \n    if (!this._eventHandlers.has(type)) {\n      this._eventHandlers.set(type, []);\n    }\n    this._eventHandlers.get(type).push(handler);\n  }\n\n  emit(type, detail) {\n    this.eventTarget.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(type, { detail }));\n  }\n\n  removeAllListeners(type) {\n    if (type) {\n      const handlers = this._eventHandlers.get(type) || [];\n      handlers.forEach(handler =&gt; {\n        this.eventTarget.removeEventListener(type, handler);\n      });\n      this._eventHandlers.delete(type);\n    } else {\n      this._eventHandlers.forEach((handlers, eventType) =&gt; {\n        handlers.forEach(handler =&gt; {\n          this.eventTarget.removeEventListener(eventType, handler);\n        });\n      });\n      this._eventHandlers.clear();\n    }\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nUsage in SmoothScroll:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript:app/components/SmoothScroll.js\nimport { EventLifecycle } from \"../utilities/EventLifecycle.js\";\n\nexport class SmoothScroll {\n  constructor(options = {}) {\n    ",
